Nio recently unveiled its first sedan, the et7, featuring self-driving technology it claims surpasses Tesla's, and is establishing itself as a premium EV brand. While homegrown EV makers saw delivery surges, their numbers still trail Tesla's, the current market leader.

title: World’s top maker of tiny motors has sights on Tesla as EVs gather pace
summary: Nidec Corp., the leading supplier of motors globally, is aiming to become a key component provider for Tesla's electric vehicles. Nidec's president, Jun Seki, expressed a strong desire to collaborate with Elon Musk, stating that Tesla would not meet its 2030 production goals without external partnerships. This move highlights Nidec's confidence in its ability to produce EV components more cheaply and effectively than competitors.

title: Spotify Bets Big on Podcasts as a Path to Profitability
summary: Spotify is facing profitability challenges due to its business model, which dedicates over 70% of its revenue to rights holders, preventing it from making a profit since its inception despite high sales. CEO Daniel Ek believes that podcasts, exemplified by investments in major creators like Joe Rogan, offer a crucial path to profitability by diversifying content beyond music and shifting away from reliance on traditional record labels. This strategy aims to give Spotify more control over content costs and attract more users, thereby securing its financial future.

title: General Motors' stock hits all-time high after Consumer Electronics Show
summary: General Motors' stock reached an all-time high of nearly $51 after the company showcased aggressive electric and autonomous vehicle plans at the Consumer Electronics Show. Analysts are cautiously optimistic that GM's focus on EVs, new battery technology (Ultium), and ventures like BrightDrop could lead to sustained stock growth, contrasting with its previous struggles since emerging from bankruptcy. The company aims to invest $27 billion in EVs and AVs, launching 30 new EVs globally by 2025.

title: China Mulls Giving Green Light to Highway Self-Driving Car Tests
summary: China is considering a draft plan to allow self-driving car tests on highways, responding to industry demand to broaden testing scenarios. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's proposal would permit vehicles that have completed extensive road tests without incident to apply for highway testing. This move could also lead to a nationwide regulatory system where test results from one region are recognized across others.

title: 5 reasons General Motors' shares are trading at all-time highs
summary: General Motors' shares reached all-time highs due to investor confidence in its future business plans, particularly in electric vehicles (EVs). CEO Mary Barra outlined ambitious strategies at the CES technology conference, including a $27 billion investment in EV and autonomous vehicle technology, introducing the BrightDrop commercial EV division, and showcasing an electric air taxi concept. The company's Ultium battery system and continued development in autonomous vehicles also contribute to the positive market outlook.

title: Weak lithium prices could slow EV revolution, Albemarle warns
summary: Albemarle, a leading lithium producer, has warned that low lithium prices could impede the expansion of supply needed for electric vehicle (EV) batteries, potentially slowing the EV revolution. The company stated that prices need to increase by at least 10% to make new expansions financially viable, despite a projected demand increase that could outstrip supply significantly by 2025. Albemarle is also exploring new production methods, such as extracting lithium from clay reserves, in anticipation of growing demand.

title: U.S. vehicle safety agency asks Tesla to recall 158,716 older vehicles over touchscreen glitches
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has requested Tesla recall 158,716 Model S and Model X vehicles produced before 2019 due to touchscreen failures. This issue, stemming from a memory device with a limited "write cycle" in the media control unit, can lead to the loss of safety-related features like rearview cameras and defrost systems. Failure rates are projected to increase with vehicle age, with all 2018 models expected to fail within 10 years.

title: Chinese driverless car start-up WeRide raises $310 million in funding as competition heats up
summary: Chinese driverless car start-up WeRide has successfully raised $310 million in a new funding round, led by Yutong Group, as it intensifies its efforts to commercialize its autonomous driving technology. This funding round follows a similar cash injection into rival Pony.ai and highlights the fierce competition within China's driverless car market, which also includes major players like Baidu and Didi. WeRide plans to launch trial operations for "Mini Robobuses" soon and anticipates large-scale robotaxi applications and profitability within the next few years.

title: NHTSA urging Tesla to recall 158,000 cars for touchscreen safety defect
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is pressuring Tesla to recall 158,000 vehicles over concerns about faulty touchscreen displays in certain Model S and Model X cars. These failures can disable crucial safety features like backup cameras and defroster controls. NHTSA has given Tesla until January 27 to respond, threatening a public hearing if the automaker doesn't address the issue.

title: Bus maker leads $310m funding for China self-drive startup WeRide
summary: Chinese autonomous vehicle startup WeRide has secured $310 million in funding, led by bus manufacturer Zhengzhou Yutong Group and other state-backed investors. This investment comes as Beijing initiates new guidelines for self-driving car testing. WeRide is also set to commence testing its autonomous buses in Guangzhou this week.

title: 3 stocks for climate transition
summary: Jaime Ramos Martin, co-portfolio manager for Aviva Investors' Climate Transition Global Equity Fund, discusses three stocks included in the fund: Union Pacific, Trane Technologies, and Volkswagen. These companies are identified as key players in the decarbonization of the economy and adaptation to climate change. Martin explains how each company, ranging from freight rail to efficient HVAC systems and electric vehicles, contributes to climate transition goals.

title: Tesla (TSLA) launches its own solar power inverter
summary: Tesla (TSLA) has launched its own solar power inverter, completing its home solar offering alongside the Powerwall and solar roof tiles. This move leverages Tesla's power electronics expertise to integrate its solar ecosystem further, offering models with 3.8 kW and 7.6 kW power outputs and 97.5% efficiency. The new inverter features Wi-Fi, Ethernet, cellular connectivity with over-the-air updates, and is designed to integrate with the Tesla Powerwall and app.

title: Monterey Bay power plant now a record-breaking battery project to ward off blackouts
summary: The former fossil fuel-burning power plant in Moss Landing, Monterey County, is being converted into a massive battery storage facility by Vistra Corp. This new project, expected to become the world's largest at 300 megawatts, will help California's energy grid by storing excess solar power and releasing it during peak demand, thereby mitigating the risk of blackouts. Alongside Vistra's project, PG&E and Tesla are also developing a substantial battery system at an adjacent substation, further contributing to grid reliability and the state's transition to cleaner energy.

title: Digital Realty moves headquarters to low-tax Texas
summary: Digital Realty, a data center REIT, has moved its corporate headquarters from San Francisco, California, to Austin, Texas, following other tech companies like Oracle and HPE. This move is influenced by Texas's lower corporate tax rate of one percent compared to California's 8.84 percent, as well as the absence of individual income tax and a lower cost of living. CEO A. William Stein and several executives have already relocated, with the company maintaining a significant presence in the Bay Area while expanding its office space and data center footprint in Texas.

title: The bull chasing the bandit: Webull takes on Robinhood
summary: This article discusses how Webull, a Chinese-owned digital brokerage, is gaining traction in the US market as a competitor to Robinhood. Webull differentiates itself with a more professional platform, in-depth data, desktop support, and live customer service, appealing to seasoned investors while Robinhood faces regulatory challenges and criticism for its "gamification" of investing. Despite being Chinese-owned, Webull has largely flown under the regulatory radar due to its proactive government relations and low-key marketing strategy.

title: Feeling Bullish? Amplify Your Investment with the SPXL ETF
summary: This article discusses the Direxion Daily S&P 500® Bull 3X Shares ETF (SPXL) as a tool for bullish traders to amplify investment in the S&P 500 amidst economic recovery and a lack of short interest in ETFs. It highlights SPXL's 25% jump over three months, reflecting growing investor confidence in a stock market recovery. The article also notes how falling short interest indicates increasing faith in a stock rally and diminishing concerns about market downside in the near future.

title: New Year, Same Story: Tesla and ARKK Still on Fire
summary: The ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) continues its strong performance from the previous year, significantly driven by its substantial investment in Tesla (TSLA). Analyst Dan Ives recently increased his target price for Tesla, citing the company's continuous advancements in electric vehicle technology and its dominant position in the EV market. ARKK, now the largest actively managed ETF by assets, has already seen a nearly 14% gain early in 2021.

title: Tesla launches a standalone solar inverter, challenging Enphase and SolarEdge for market share
summary: Tesla has introduced its first standalone solar inverter, available in 3.8kW and 7.8kW capacities, featuring multiple maximum power point trackers. This move positions Tesla as a direct competitor to Enphase and SolarEdge in the inverter market, allowing the company more control over the cost of its solar systems and offering complete product verticality for solar installations.

title: ARK Investment Plans to Augment Offerings with a Space ETF
summary: ARK Investment, led by Cathie Wood, plans to launch a new actively managed space-focused ETF to invest in domestic and foreign companies engaged in space exploration and innovation. This follows the firm's significant success with its existing disruptive technology ETFs. The article discusses potential holdings like Virgin Galactic and defense contractors, and the broader impact on mainstream investments in the space sector, especially considering a potential indirect exposure to SpaceX IPO.

title: Tesla’s Advanced Battery Research group gets new leadership, Jeff Dahn to become advisor for Novonix
summary: Professor Jeff Dahn, a renowned battery researcher who has had an exclusive partnership with Tesla since 2016 through Dalhousie University, is stepping down from his leadership role at Tesla’s Advanced Battery Research group. He will now serve as Chief Scientific Advisor at Novonix Battery Technology Solutions, a company spun out from his research group. Dahn and his team will continue working with Tesla, which has extended its contract with the Dalhousie University group until 2026, welcoming two new chairs to lead research into advanced Li-ion battery materials and performance.

title: Tesla’s Autopilot Won’t Achieve Full Autonomy, Waymo CEO Says
summary: The CEO of Waymo, John Krafcik, stated in an interview that Tesla's Autopilot will not achieve full autonomy, calling its development approach "misguided." He criticized the idea that a driver assistance system can magically evolve into a fully autonomous one and emphasized that Waymo does not consider Tesla a competitor in the driverless vehicle space, instead viewing their system as a "really good driver assistance system." This comes despite Tesla CEO Elon Musk's past claims about achieving full autonomy.

title: BorgWarner to Supply Transfer Cases for Nissan SUV and Pick-up
summary: BorgWarner has secured a contract to supply its part-time transfer cases to Nissan for their Navara pick-up and Paladin SUV models. This is the first time BorgWarner will supply transfer cases to Nissan, strengthening their relationship. The advanced two-speed, shift-on-the-fly system offers quick and accurate shifting between 2WD high, 4WD high, and 4WD low modes, improving vehicle dynamics and performance.

title: CarParts.com Launches First Electric Vehicle & Hybrid Focused Shopping Hub
summary: CarParts.com has launched a new online shopping hub specifically for hybrid and electric vehicle (EV) parts, featuring over 700,000 applications for various popular makes. This initiative aims to address misconceptions about EV and hybrid repairs and provide a comprehensive resource for owners as these vehicles become older and require aftermarket parts. The company emphasizes its commitment to becoming the leading online destination for the EV community, offering parts, information, and tools.

title: Which Chinese EV Stocks Are Worth Betting On
summary: Despite a slow start to the year for oil prices due to COVID-19 concerns, the EV sector continues its strong performance, with Chinese EV companies showing significant gains. This article highlights three Chinese EV manufacturers—XPeng Motors, NIO Limited, and Li Auto—as promising investment opportunities, detailing their market performance, financial health, and innovative strategies.

title: Tesla's report could trigger $7 billion payout to Musk
summary: Tesla's upcoming quarterly report could lead to a $7 billion options payout for CEO Elon Musk if the company's adjusted EBITDA reaches $2.3 billion, triggering the vesting of a fifth tranche from his 2018 pay package. Investors are also keenly awaiting Tesla's 2021 delivery target after the company's stock soared nearly 700% in the past year, making it the fifth-most-valuable publicly traded U.S. company. The company's market capitalization now stands at $843 billion, despite producing a fraction of the vehicles compared to traditional automakers.

title: Baron Partners' Huge Tesla Stake Leads to Downgrade
summary: Baron Partners fund has been downgraded to a Morningstar Analyst Rating of Neutral from Bronze due to its highly concentrated stake in Tesla, which grew to 47% of net assets. Despite lead manager Ron Baron selling some shares and reducing overall fund leverage, the stock's meteoric rise disproportionately influenced the fund's risk profile, highlighting lax risk controls. This concentration, while leading to significant returns in 2020, introduces substantial volatility and risk.

title: Fort Lauderdale Tunnel Could Be ‘Game Changer' for Traffic Issues: Mayor
summary: Fort Lauderdale Mayor Dean Trantalis believes a proposed three-mile tunnel under the New River, built by Elon Musk's The Boring Company, could be a "game changer" for the city's traffic issues and help establish South Florida as a tech hub. The project, estimated at a minimum of $10 million per mile, could also extend commuter lines to suburbs and beaches. The idea gained national attention after discussions between Musk and Miami Mayor Francis Suarez, with Trantalis planning further talks with Boring Company representatives to assess ground topography.

title: AI fund that's beating S&P 500 has shifted into tech stocks
summary: A machine-guided fund, the AI Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ), has significantly shifted its holdings into technology stocks, now comprising over 37% of its portfolio. This move comes as the fund continues to outperform the S&P 500 Index, having risen 12% this year compared to the S&P 500's nearly 3% gain. The fund has also halved its industrial exposure and doubled its position in Tesla Inc., while significantly reducing its Apple Inc. holdings.

title: STMicroelectronics, Tesla and Apple: what happens when eMobility & 5G collide
summary: This article examines how STMicroelectronics' Q4 2020 results were bolstered by its key relationships with Tesla in e-mobility and Apple in 5G mobile and consumer markets. It highlights STMicroelectronics' dominance in Silicon Carbide (SiC) for electric vehicles, largely driven by Tesla's adoption, and its significant role in CMOS image sensors for Apple's 3D imaging and sensing applications. The article also discusses the company's strategies to address capacity constraints and maintain its market position against competitors.

title: GameStop stock market surge captures attention, enriches Michigan billionaire Donald Foss
summary: The article details the significant surge in GameStop's stock price, highlighting how it substantially increased the wealth of Michigan billionaire Donald Foss, who held a 5.3% stake. It describes the phenomenon as a battle between day traders and Wall Street short sellers, driven by activity on Reddit, and notes the skepticism of financial analysts regarding the company's underlying fundamentals. The piece also mentions the broader market impact, the involvement of figures like Elon Musk, and warnings about the irrationality of the market.

title: GM's all-electric pledge: No tailpipes by 2035, net-zero carbon by 2040
summary: General Motors announced its intention to achieve net-zero carbon status by 2040, with an aspiration to eliminate tailpipe emissions from new light-duty vehicles by 2035. The company plans to introduce 30 all-electric models globally by mid-decade and aims for 40% of its U.S. models to be battery electric vehicles by the end of 2025. This commitment is supported by a $27 billion investment in electric and autonomous vehicles over the next five years, and a push for 100% renewable energy in its facilities by 2030 in the U.S. and 2035 globally.

title: UVXY ETF Is a Good Buy as Earnings and WSB Drive Volatility
summary: The article discusses why the ProShares Ultra VIX Short-Term Futures ETF (UVXY) is a good buy amidst rising market volatility. It explains that the VIX Index, which UVXY tracks, is rising due to the earnings season, fears of a stock market bubble, and the impact of the WallStreetBets Reddit community on certain stocks. The article suggests UVXY as a way to bet on continued volatility given its asset size, liquidity, and expense ratio compared to competitors.

title: General Motors plans to exclusively offer electric vehicles by 2035
summary: General Motors announced its aspiration to exclusively offer electric vehicles by 2035, ending the production of gasoline- and diesel-powered cars, trucks, and SUVs. This move is part of the company's broader plan to become carbon neutral by 2040 in its global products and operations, and comes a day after President Joe Biden signed executive orders prioritizing climate change. GM also plans to use 100% renewable energy for its U.S. facilities by 2030 and global facilities by 2035.

title: General Motors Aims To Be Carbon Neutral By 2040
summary: General Motors announced its goal to achieve carbon neutrality by 2040, including eliminating tailpipe emissions from light-duty vehicles by 2035. The company plans to take a science-based approach and have 40% of its vehicles be battery-powered by 2025. GM also aims to power its U.S. sites with 100% renewable energy by 2030 and globally by 2035, while working with EVgo to expand fast-charging infrastructure.

title: In a Major Move Away From Fossil Fuels, General Motors Aims to Stop Selling Gasoline Cars and SUVs by 2035
summary: General Motors announced its intention to stop selling gasoline and diesel vehicles by 2035, aligning with a broader plan to achieve carbon neutrality by 2040. This significant shift by the largest U.S. automaker is driven by technological advancements making electric vehicles more affordable and a global trend towards stricter emissions regulations. While presenting a gamble for GM, the move is seen as a strategic response to evolving market conditions and policy targets set by governments like California and the Biden administration.

title: GM to only sell zero-emissions models by 2035
summary: General Motors announced a bold pledge to make all its global operations and vehicles carbon neutral by 2040, including selling only zero-emission models by 2035. This move aligns with California's emission-reduction goals and places GM ahead of rivals like Ford in its carbon neutrality target. CEO Mary Barra's strategy aims to challenge Tesla's electric vehicle dominance and reshape GM's image, investing $27 billion into 30 electric vehicles by 2025.

title: CarParts.com Launches First EV, Hybrid-Focused Shopping Hub
summary: CarParts.com has introduced a dedicated shopping hub for hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and electric vehicle (EV) owners, expanding its product offerings to over 700,000 applications. The new platform aims to simplify the search for maintenance and repair parts, addressing misconceptions that EV and hybrid parts are vastly different from those for gas-powered cars. With a growing number of older EVs and hybrids on the road, CarParts.com is investing in its infrastructure to become a leading online destination for the EV community.

title: How Tesla made it to the top
summary: Tesla, co-founded by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning, was initially conceived to build high-performance electric sports cars using lithium-ion batteries. Despite facing near-bankruptcy and production challenges, Elon Musk took over as CEO in 2008 and spearheaded its growth. The company differentiated itself by integrating its entire supply chain, avoiding traditional advertising, and aiming for a global transition to clean energy, ultimately becoming the world's most valuable car company, though it now faces increasing competition from other major automakers entering the EV market.

title: GM’s all-EV plan could shake the energy industry
summary: General Motors announced its plan to stop making gas-powered cars by 2035 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2040, a move expected to transform the electric vehicle market and energy industry. This significant commitment will necessitate dramatic changes to the electric grid and put GM in direct competition with Tesla. The shift also marks a major policy turnaround for GM, which previously sided with the Trump administration against stricter emissions standards.

title: GM looks to sell only emission-free vehicles by 2035
summary: General Motors announced its ambitious plan to become carbon neutral by 2040 and aims to offer only zero-emissions vehicles by 2035. This transition involves a significant investment of $27 billion and a commitment to source 100% renewable energy for its global plants by 2035, accelerating its previous timeline. While the 2035 goal for zero-emissions vehicles is stated as an "aspiration," GM is heavily investing in electric vehicle manufacturing and aligning with new Biden administration climate initiatives.

title: How To Invest In Hydrogen
summary: This article explores investment opportunities in the burgeoning hydrogen economy, highlighting the distinction between "green," "blue," and "grey" hydrogen based on production methods and environmental impact. It emphasizes government support and growing consumer interest as key drivers for this sector, while also cautioning about potentially high valuations of related companies. The author provides lists of companies active in hydrogen, underscoring the importance of understanding specific applications and production processes.

title: EV firm Microvast to go public through $3 billion merger with SPAC
summary: Electric-vehicle battery maker Microvast announced it would go public through a merger with blank-check company Tuscan Holdings Corp, valuing the combined entity at roughly $3 billion. Microvast will receive $822 million in gross cash proceeds, including a $540 million private investment. The company, founded in 2006, previously powered electric buses for the 2018 Winter Olympic Games.

title: Nio Stock Could Pull Back To $50 Before Surging To $70 Long-Term
summary: Nio stock experienced a significant surge in the past year due to the electric vehicle (EV) market boom, but a pullback to around $50 is anticipated before a potential long-term rally to $70. The company reported strong Q3 earnings with increased deliveries and positive cash flow, though much of the good news may already be priced into the stock. Investors are advised to consider investing after a dip or use strategies like covered calls to hedge positions given potential volatility and overbought technical indicators.

title: Nestle, Nvidia, and the Changing Global Equity Markets
summary: The article analyzes the shifting dynamics of global equity markets over the past decade, characterized by the dominance of U.S. technology stocks like Nvidia, in contrast to traditional companies like Nestle. It highlights the increased concentration of U.S. market indexes in technology and consumer cyclical sectors, and discusses current valuation opportunities in non-U.S. markets and value sectors like energy.

title: Chip shortage hits General Motors production
summary: General Motors announced it will cut production at three North American factories and half capacity at one in South Korea due to a global semiconductor chip shortage. This comes as chipmaker Qualcomm also reported that supply constraints are hampering its sales growth. The shortage is impacting several other automakers, and projections suggest the issue could last into the third quarter of the year.

title: Elon Musk admits Tesla has quality problems
summary: Elon Musk has acknowledged Tesla's quality issues, particularly during new model production ramp-ups, confirming criticisms from engineering consultant Sandy Munro. Munro, who initially criticized the Model 3's quality in 2018, noted significant improvements in later production runs. Musk advised customers to either buy a Tesla at the very beginning of a model's run or once production has stabilized to avoid early quality challenges.

title: Tennessee Highways Put EV Charging Stations Every 50 Miles
summary: Tennessee is launching a new initiative to install fast-charging stations for electric vehicles every 50 miles along its major highways. This $20 million program, funded by Volkswagen emission penalties and contributions from TVA and local power companies, aims to build 50 new stations over the next three to five years, more than doubling the current number. The goal is to alleviate "range anxiety" for EV drivers and support Tennessee's target of having 200,000 light-duty electric vehicles by 2028, aligning with the state's growing EV manufacturing sector.

title: Allegro Microsystems sees record revenue in first post-IPO report
summary: Allegro MicroSystems reported record revenue of $164.4 million in its first quarter as a publicly traded company, exceeding expectations and driven largely by a strong rebound in the automotive industry. Automotive revenue accounted for 69% of the total, growing 27% from the prior quarter, with additional growth from industrial revenue and new design wins expected to contribute to future sales. The company's stock, which debuted at $14 a share, closed at $29.02, reflecting investor confidence.

title: The BOTZ Are Coming. But So Are Investing Gains
summary: The Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence Thematic ETF (BOTZ) has seen a 60% increase in the past year, driven by companies like Japanese robot maker Fanuc Corp, which boosted its profit forecast due to rising demand for electric cars. BOTZ invests in companies benefiting from robotics and AI adoption, offering high growth potential and exposure to an emerging theme. The growing electric vehicle industry, supported by President Biden's clean energy agenda, provides significant tailwinds for BOTZ and its holdings.

title: Ford posts $1.3 billion loss, ups EV spending, warns of microchip shortage
summary: Ford Motor Co. reported a $1.3 billion loss for 2020 and a $2.8 billion net loss in Q4 due to coronavirus-dampened sales and production disruptions. In response, Ford is increasing its investments in electric and autonomous vehicles to over $22 billion and $7 billion respectively through 2025. The company also warned of further headwinds from a global microchip shortage impacting its most profitable vehicles.

title: Tesla to recall 36,126 Model S and X vehicles in China over touch-screen failures
summary: Tesla is recalling 36,126 Model S and Model X vehicles in China due to touch-screen failures, stemming from limited "write cycle" memory devices. This follows a similar recall in the U.S. and an investigation in Germany for the same issue, as Tesla agreed to replace the affected memory devices with a 64 GB version. China is a significant market for Tesla, where it held a 12% share of the "new energy vehicle" category in 2020.

title: Tesla founders Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning talk about the early days and bringing on Elon Musk
summary: Tesla founders Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning recount the early days of Tesla, challenging the popular belief that Elon Musk started the company. They discuss building and delivering the first Tesla Roadster, convincing the market about electric cars, and how Elon Musk became involved. Despite later contention with Musk, Eberhard and Tarpenning remain supportive of Tesla's mission and reflect positively on their contributions.

title: Solar-Powered Charging Stations Are Vital to Promoting EVs
summary: Electrify America has installed 30 new free-to-use, off-grid solar-powered EV charging stations in rural California to promote EV adoption outside major cities. These stations, sourced from Beam Global (formerly Envision Solar), are designed to address the lack of accessible EV infrastructure in rural areas. They provide a reliable charging solution, especially important during grid outages, and aim to reduce range anxiety for potential EV buyers in underserved regions.

title: Tesla Bets on Bitcoin in Blue-Chip Boost to Cryptocurrency
summary: Tesla Inc. announced a $1.5 billion investment in Bitcoin and stated its intention to accept the cryptocurrency as a form of payment. This move by the electric-car maker caused Bitcoin prices to surge to a record high. The investment signals a significant endorsement of cryptocurrency from a major blue-chip company.

title: A Look At 6 ETFs That Cover The Electric Vehicles Trend
summary: This article discusses the accelerating growth of the global electric vehicle (EV) market, highlighting record sales in late 2020 and forecasts for exponential growth from 2022 onwards. It recommends six electric vehicle-related ETFs, four of which cover EVs plus autonomous vehicles (AVs) and two that focus on EVs plus the EV supply chain, including battery makers and miners. The author emphasizes that the real EV boom has just begun and provides sales figures and market share percentages to support this trend.

title: Tesla (TSLA) Discloses $1.5B Investment in Bitcoin
summary: Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) announced a $1.5 billion investment in Bitcoin and plans to accept Bitcoin payments for its cars, making it the first S&P 500 company to invest in the cryptocurrency. This move follows a change in its investment policy to diversify and maximize returns on cash. The announcement propelled Bitcoin's price to new record highs, reflecting CEO Elon Musk's bullish stance and broader corporate and retail interest in the asset.

title: Tesla skips 401(k) match for third straight year
summary: Tesla has reportedly skipped its 401(k) match for the third consecutive year. This information was reported in an article by Rob Kozlowski on February 8, 2021, at 3:43 PM EST. The move impacts employees who rely on employer contributions to their retirement savings plans.

title: Why BTBT Stock Should Be in Your Portfolio
summary: Bit Digital (BTBT) is a blockchain company focused on bitcoin mining, and its stock price is heavily influenced by bitcoin's value. The article suggests BTBT stock could continue to rise due to growing investor interest in cryptocurrency and bitcoin's fixed supply. It also compares BTBT favorably to Riot Blockchain and highlights the growing adoption of blockchain technology.

title: Tesla Bets Big on Bitcoin, Starves its 401(k) Plan
summary: Tesla announced a $1.5 billion investment in Bitcoin and plans to accept the cryptocurrency as payment, pushing Bitcoin to record highs. Despite this progressive financial move and significant stock growth, Tesla's 401(k) plan has received no company contributions for several years, offering a "pedestrian" plan to its employees. However, the company provides stock options to all employees, which have led to substantial gains for many, potentially offsetting the lack of traditional 401(k) matching.

title: Tesla existed before Elon Musk: Founders on how they pitched the idea
summary: This article details how Tesla was founded by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning in 2003, before Elon Musk's involvement. It covers their initial concept for the Tesla Roadster, their pitch to Lotus, and how they secured Musk's investment. The piece also touches on the co-founders' eventual departure from the company and their subsequent careers.

title: Why did Tesla buy bitcoin?
summary: The article discusses Tesla Inc.'s recent investment in bitcoin, highlighting it as a significant move that underscores the increasing acceptance of the digital asset. It raises the central question observers are asking: why did Elon Musk's company make this investment?

title: General Motors made $6.4 billion in 2020, despite COVID-19
summary: General Motors reported a profit of $6.43 billion in 2020, despite a 4.5% fall from the previous year, driven by strong demand for trucks and SUVs in the latter half of the year. The company is facing new challenges, including an estimated $1.5 billion to $2 billion loss due to a global semiconductor chip shortage in 2021, but anticipates pretax income of $10 billion to $11 billion for the year. GM also unveiled plans to invest over $7 billion in electric and self-driving vehicles in 2021 as part of its broader push into EVs.

title: Bitcoin hits record highs as more companies embrace crypto boom
summary: Bitcoin reached new record highs following announcements from Mastercard Inc. and Bank of New York Mellon Corp. about their increased embrace of cryptocurrencies. This surge is further fueled by Tesla CEO Elon Musk's significant investment in Bitcoin and his public support for cryptocurrencies, attracting more traditional financial institutions to the digital asset class. Despite the growing adoption, critics continue to warn of speculative bubbles and potential misuse.

title: Toyota Launching Two New EVs, One New Plug-In Hybrid—and Soon
summary: Toyota plans to introduce two new battery-powered electric vehicles and one plug-in hybrid in 2021, set to hit the market in 2022, specifically for the U.S. market. The company emphasizes a mixed electrified vehicle strategy, continuing to sell a combination of hybrids, plug-in hybrids, and pure battery electric vehicles to most effectively reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Toyota highlights that a single approach to electrification doesn't fit all customers, promoting different solutions based on individual circumstances, unlike some competitors moving directly to all-electric lineups.

title: BNY Mellon to offer bitcoin services, a validation of crypto from a key bank in the financial system
summary: BNY Mellon, the oldest bank in the U.S., announced it will begin financing bitcoin and other digital currencies, integrating them into its existing financial network. This move marks a significant validation for the crypto market from a major custodian bank, driven by growing client demand and improved regulatory clarity. The announcement led to a 2% rise in BNY Mellon's shares and follows a robust start to 2021 for Bitcoin, which was up 7.7% to around $48,250 on the news.

title: Toyota Will Bring Two EVs to the U.S. This Year
summary: Toyota plans to introduce two new battery-electric vehicles and a plug-in hybrid in the U.S. this year, marking a significant commitment to electrification after showing prior skepticism. The company aims to have 40% of its U.S. lineup be electrified by 2025 and 70% by 2030, leveraging its e-TNGA platform for new sedan and compact SUV EV models. Despite being a hybrid pioneer, Toyota is now working to catch up with other automakers in the pure EV market while continuing to explore hydrogen technology.

title: Biden SEC Nominee Gary Gensler Worth as Much as $119 Million
summary: Gary Gensler, President Joe Biden’s nominee for SEC chairman, has disclosed a net worth between $41 million and $119 million. This information came from a government ethics form filed as part of his confirmation process. Gensler's past holdings included Tesla and a pension payout from Goldman Sachs.

title: First Trust NASDAQ Clean Edge Smart Grid Infrastructure Index Fund (GRID) Stock Price, Quote, News & History
summary: This article provides a comprehensive overview of the First Trust NASDAQ Clean Edge Smart Grid Infrastructure Index Fund (GRID), including its stock price, key statistics, news, and history. It details the fund's holdings, dividend information, and investment policy, explaining its focus on companies involved in smart grid infrastructure. The article also includes FAQs about buying GRID stock, competitors, price targets, and earning schedules.

title: Tesla to set up electric car manufacturing unit in southern India
summary: Tesla Inc. plans to establish an electric car manufacturing unit in Karnataka, a southern Indian state, according to a government document. This move follows the incorporation of Tesla Motors India and Energy Private Limited in Bengaluru last month. The company's CEO, Elon Musk, has previously indicated Tesla's entry into India in 2021 as the country seeks to electrify its transport sector.

title: Churchill Capital IV soars 33% after report says the SPAC is nearing a deal to take EV maker Lucid Motors public
summary: Churchill Capital Corp IV (CCIV) stock surged 33% after Reuters reported that the SPAC is close to a deal to take electric vehicle manufacturer Lucid Motors public with a $12 billion valuation. This news is a confirmation of rumors that began in January, which had already caused CCIV's shares to jump significantly. The potential merger would add Lucid to a growing list of EV companies going public via SPACs, a trend that has seen mixed results for investors.

title: In Depth: The 1,000 Kilometer Target Driving China’s Electric Car Industry Into a Frenzy
summary: Chinese EV manufacturers are intensely pursuing a 1,000-kilometer driving range on a single charge to entice consumers away from gas-powered cars, with companies like Nio promising cutting-edge solid-state batteries. However, experts caution that achieving this target with current technology involves significant tradeoffs in safety, cost, and overall eco-friendliness. The article points out that focusing solely on range might overlook other critical factors like charging infrastructure and affordable mini-EVs, which are already proving popular in the market.

title: South Florida Mayors to Visit Vegas, LA Test Tunnel for Local Commuter Rail
summary: Mayors from Miami and Fort Lauderdale are traveling to the West Coast to examine Elon Musk's Boring Company tunnel technology in Las Vegas and California. Their goal is to assess whether this low-cost tunneling approach could be a viable solution for building underground commuter rail in South Florida, addressing traffic congestion and infrastructure challenges like the New River issue. The Boring Company has already expressed interest in collaborating with Fort Lauderdale officials on potential applications.

Origin Materials, a startup creating sustainable plastic from sawdust, is going public through a SPAC merger with Artius Acquisition in a $1.8 billion deal. The company aims to replace petroleum-based plastics with carbon-negative materials, having already secured partnerships with major brands like Danone, Nestle, and PepsiCo. This transaction is expected to fully fund Origin Materials until it achieves EBITDA and free cash flow positive status by 2025, enabling the construction of its first full-scale commercial plant.

title: Elon Musk may be betting on Bitcoin—but here’s what 50 other CFOs really think about it
summary: A survey by Gartner Finance revealed that 95% of CFOs have no plans to purchase Bitcoin in the current year, despite Elon Musk's investment. While corporate America's curiosity about Bitcoin is growing, its volatility and cash management problems deter most finance leaders, who prioritize financial stability. However, 5% of companies plan to buy Bitcoin this year, and a larger percentage anticipate doing so in the future, with board risk aversion being less of a concern than expected.

title: Chrysler, Buick make top 10 in Consumer Reports' auto brand ranking
summary: The Chrysler and Buick brands significantly improved their standing in Consumer Reports' Brand Report Card Rankings, both moving into the top 10 out of 32 brands. This marks only the second time two Detroit auto brands have reached the top 10. Despite this, no Detroit Three vehicle made the annual "Top Picks" list for 2021.

title: How ST is driving Tesla and Apple e-mobility and 5G ambitions
summary: STMicroelectronics' success is heavily reliant on its key customers, Tesla and Apple. For Tesla, STMicroelectronics is a leading supplier of Silicon Carbide (SiC) power devices for e-mobility, particularly traction inverters, despite capacity constraints which ST is addressing through acquisitions and R&D. For Apple, STMicroelectronics makes significant contributions to 3D imaging and sensing, including NIR image sensors and Time of Flight detectors for iPhones, though Sony's increasing presence in Apple devices poses a potential challenge for STMicroelectronics' future in the CMOS image sensor market.

title: Tesla sticker shock: Automaker slashes prices for two models
summary: Tesla has reduced prices for its Model 3 Standard Range Plus and Model Y Standard Range by 2.6% and 4.8% respectively, while increasing prices for the Performance variants of both models. CEO Elon Musk has previously stated that Tesla's cars are too expensive, and the company frequently uses price adjustments to boost deliveries. This strategy, supported by cost cuts, aims to increase volume, according to analysts.

title: Tesla cuts Model 3 prices in Japan by as much as 24%
summary: Tesla has significantly reduced the prices of its Model 3 vehicles in Japan, with cuts reaching as high as 24%. This move comes as the company attempts to boost sales in the Japanese market. The price adjustments affect various configurations of the Model 3 lineup.

title: Chief executive of Japan's Honda to step down, hand reins to R&D chief
summary: Takahiro Hachigo, CEO of Honda Motor Co., will step down on April 1 and be replaced by Toshihiro Mibe, the current head of research and development. Mibe's appointment comes as Honda accelerates its efforts in electric vehicle development amid fierce competition. Analysts believe this leadership change will help Honda accelerate its electrification strategy.

title: Elon Musk explains Tesla's $1.5B bitcoin buy
summary: Elon Musk explained that Tesla's decision to buy $1.5 billion of Bitcoin was motivated by the inability to get a return on the company's cash when fiat currency yields negative real interest. He also noted that "Bitcoin is almost as bs as fiat money," agreeing with MicroStrategy CEO Michael Saylor. Tesla plans to accept Bitcoin for car payments and may invest further in digital assets.

title: The man charged with keeping SolarEdge’s current flowing
summary: SolarEdge CEO Zvi Lando discusses the company's valuation spike to $18 billion, its expansion into new renewable energy sectors, and the challenge of stepping into the role previously held by the late founder Guy Sella. He also addresses issues like the impact of Elon Musk's Tesla announcement on SolarEdge's stock and the company's commitment to remaining Israeli despite global operations.

title: The Future of Texas (Published 2021)
summary: Texas has strong economic prospects due to its affordability, cultural appeal, diverse population, and strong educational system, leading to significant population growth and corporate relocations. However, its reliance on fossil fuels poses long-term threats from climate change, such as increased extreme weather and the vulnerability of its infrastructure, as recent power outages demonstrated. The state's political actions have also hindered climate change mitigation efforts nationally.

title: Since Three-Phase Motors Mean Triple the Components, TI Banks on Integration
summary: Texas Instruments has released a highly-integrated 48V motor driver, the DRV3255-Q1, designed to reduce PCB area by up to 30% in mild-hybrid electric vehicles (MHEVs). This single IC integrates components typically found in three separate driver circuits for three-phase motors, aiming to lower BOM, cost, and improve signal integrity. The innovation seeks to accelerate MHEV adoption by making them more affordable, safer, and greener while addressing the increasing demand for electrification.

title: Battery Maker Enovix to IPO in $1.1 Billion SPAC Deal
summary: Battery maker Enovix has agreed to go public through a business combination with Rodgers Silicon Valley Acquisition Corp. (NASDAQ: RSVA) in a deal valuing Enovix at over $1.1 billion. The transaction, a reverse merger, provides Enovix with approximately $385 million in net cash and is expected to be completed in the second quarter, after which RSVA will be renamed Enovix Corporation and trade as ENVX on the Nasdaq. This move highlights the increasing popularity of SPAC reverse mergers for companies entering the public market.

title: Xos to Go Public and Expand Battery-Electric Vehicle Production
summary: Xos Inc., a battery-electric commercial vehicle manufacturer, announced its plan to go public through a business combination with NextGen Acquisition Corp., a SPAC, in a deal valuing the combined entity at $2 billion. The move is expected to raise $575 million in gross proceeds, allowing Xos to expand manufacturing, advance battery technology, and fulfill its 6,000-order backlog. Xos will also partner with Thompson Truck Centers for distribution, aiming to deliver up to 1,000 trucks over the next three years.

title: Myth-Busting Six Misconceptions about Thematic Investing
summary: This article addresses six common misconceptions about thematic investing, providing data and analysis to clarify the complexities, investor demographics, sector scope, market timing, valuations, and appropriate entry points for thematic investments. It explains Global X's rigorous approach to theme identification, methodology development, and ongoing analysis, highlighting that thematic investing is a long-term strategy that is often misunderstood.

title: Apple buys a company every three to four weeks
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook revealed that the company has acquired approximately 100 companies over the past six years, averaging one acquisition every three to four weeks. These acquisitions are primarily focused on gaining technology and talent, helping Apple to integrate innovations into its products and expand into areas like AI, self-driving technology, and payments. Despite its rapid acquisition pace, Apple tends to buy smaller firms and has been more financially restrained in its purchases compared to other big tech companies.

title: Tesla Stock Wipes Out Gains for the Year
summary: Tesla Inc. shares erased all their year-to-date gains and briefly traded below their S&P 500 entry level, experiencing a significant intraday decline. This drop was influenced by CEO Elon Musk's comments on cryptocurrency valuations and Tesla's decision to halt orders for its lowest-priced Model Y, amid increasing competition from traditional automakers in the EV market.

title: Foreign brands' adventures in localization for the China market
summary: Foreign brands, particularly KFC, are increasingly localizing their products and marketing strategies to cater to the unique tastes and cultural preferences of the Chinese market. This approach has proven highly successful, enabling companies to capture significant market share and attract Chinese consumers. The robust and growing Chinese consumer market continues to be a major draw for foreign investment, despite global economic challenges.

title: Lucid Motors 'humbly' embarks on the difficult task of mass producing its electric cars, CEO says
summary: Lucid Motors CEO Peter Rawlinson emphasized the company's commitment to "humbly and diligently execute" the mass production of its electric vehicles following a SPAC deal that valued the company at over $50 billion. Rawlinson, a former Tesla executive, highlighted Lucid's world-class technology and the challenge of scaling automobile production. The luxury Air sedan deliveries are set for the second half of 2021, with plans for an SUV in 2023 and more affordable models later, projecting significant EBITDA and vehicle deliveries by 2026.

title: What to Do When the Market Is Manic
summary: This article discusses the manic state of the current market, exemplified by events like the GameStop short squeeze, and advises investors on a contrarian approach. It highlights historically stretched valuations and low bond yields as reasons for caution, suggesting investors rebalance portfolios, de-risk fixed income, and practice "doing a whole lot of nothing" by tuning out market noise.

title: Nothing Lucid About a $57 Billion Valuation for an Electric-Vehicle Startup
summary: Lucid Motors, an electric-vehicle startup, announced a merger with SPAC Churchill Capital IV, leading to an implied market valuation of roughly $57 billion. While Lucid is seen as a strong contender to follow Tesla's success, investors are questioning the inflated valuation. The article highlights the significant increase in Churchill Capital IV's market value following reports of the merger talks.

title: For Salesforce, Corporate Growth Means Contributing to Society
summary: Salesforce.com is highlighted for its long-standing commitment to sustainability and social contribution, particularly through its 1-1-1 model. The article discusses how this philosophy, typical of Silicon Valley firms, links corporate growth with addressing societal issues, influencing competitiveness and employee diversity. Salesforce's management also leads by example, integrating SDG goals and regularly evaluating social contributions.

title: Silver's Clean Energy Future
summary: This article discusses the crucial and often underestimated role of silver in the global clean energy transition, focusing on its industrial applications in electric vehicles, solar power, and 5G technology. It highlights how growing demand from these sectors, coupled with stagnating supply, points to a highly positive future for silver prices. The author details specific silver uses and projected demand increases in each area, linking them to global decarbonization efforts and government initiatives.

title: Tesla's Elon Musk says U.S. factory closed for two days due to parts shortages
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that the company's Fremont, California plant was shut down for two days this week due to "parts shortages" but had since reopened. This closure comes as several major automakers are experiencing chip shortages, forcing them to reduce production. Musk also noted that the company was using the downtime for equipment upgrades and maintenance, and that production of the Model S and Model X lines would soon return to two shifts.

title: Powerful House Dem bought cannabis stocks after pushing decriminalization
summary: Rep. John Yarmuth, chairman of the House Budget Committee, purchased up to $60,000 worth of stock in cannabis companies shortly after pushing for the decriminalization of marijuana. While such stock purchases by members of Congress are legal under the STOCK Act if not based on non-public information, Yarmuth's investment coincided with a House bill he co-sponsored to decriminalize cannabis. This event follows other instances of Congressional members or their spouses facing scrutiny for timely investment decisions, including Paul Pelosi's Tesla options and Senators' stock sales prior to the COVID-19 market crash.

title: Toyota Develops Packaged Fuel Cell System Module to Promote the Hydrogen Utilization toward the Achievement of Carbon Neutrality
summary: Toyota has developed a compact, packaged fuel cell system module designed for easy integration into various FC products like trucks, buses, trains, ships, and stationary generators. This initiative aims to accelerate hydrogen utilization and reduce CO2 emissions, contributing to carbon neutrality. The module comes in four models, offering high versatility, reliable safety features, and excellent performance, leveraging Toyota's extensive experience in FCEV development.

title: Lomiko Moves Forward With La Loutre Graphite Development
summary: Lomiko Metals Inc. is pleased to report progress on its La Loutre Graphite Development Plans, spurred by President Biden's executive order to review U.S. supply chains for key sectors like electric vehicle batteries. The company highlights the recent mining permit approval for its neighbor, Nouveau Monde Graphite, as a positive indicator for its own development in Quebec. The article also discusses the increasing demand for natural flake graphite, particularly in the rapidly growing lithium-ion battery market for EVs, and anticipates a rise in graphite prices due to scarce supply.

title: This Chinese EV company swaps batteries instead of waiting for them to charge
summary: Nio, a Chinese EV company, is implementing a "battery-as-a-service" model where customers can buy cars without batteries and instead pay a monthly subscription. This system allows for quick battery swaps in three minutes at designated stations, aiming to make EVs more affordable and convenient, especially in urban areas where at-home charging is less common. Although battery swapping has failed in the past, Nio believes the current market is ready for this solution.

title: BTCS Drives Near-Term Revenue Growth by Expanding its Ethereum 2.0 Staking Operation to 100 Nodes
summary: BTCS Inc. announced the expansion of its Ethereum 2.0 staking operation to 100 nodes, projecting strong near-term revenue growth. The company has staked 3,200 ETH, valued at nearly $5 Million, and expects 2Q21 revenues to benefit. BTCS also highlighted its history as an early blockchain pioneer and the first U.S. public company to run validator nodes on Ethereum 2.0.

title: EXCLUSIVE Goldman Sachs restarts cryptocurrency desk amid bitcoin boom
summary: Goldman Sachs has reactivated its cryptocurrency trading desk to deal in bitcoin futures and non-deliverable forwards, driven by increasing institutional interest in digital assets. This move positions the bank within the rapidly expanding digital assets sector, which also involves exploring blockchain technology, central bank digital currencies, and the potential for a bitcoin exchange-traded fund. The decision follows bitcoin's significant price surge and broader acceptance by major companies like Tesla and Bank of New York Mellon, despite its inherent volatility.

title: Barstool's Portnoy backs new BUZZ ETF
summary: Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy announced his backing of the new BUZZ ETF, which is set to debut on the NYSE. This ETF leverages artificial intelligence to analyze social media chatter and track the top 75 large-cap stocks with market capitalizations over $5 billion. Portnoy, who holds an ownership stake in BUZZ, highlighted that the algorithm outperformed the S&P 500 by 40% in 2020.

title: Electric Vehicles on the Rise: Should You Invest in the EV Market?
summary: The article explores the rapidly growing electric vehicle (EV) market and discusses investment opportunities. It advises considering the entire supply chain, from manufacturers to charging infrastructure and rare earth elements, while also cautioning against stock bubbles and highlighting potential risks and benefits of various EV companies and ETFs.

title: How Battery Metals Have Helped Us Outperform During the Slump in Gold Price
summary: Despite a slump in gold prices, U.S. Global Investors' World Precious Minerals Fund (UNWPX) has outperformed peers by strategically investing in battery metals like lithium, copper, nickel, cobalt, and graphite. The article highlights the strong investment case for these materials due to record-setting money printing, rising inflation expectations, and the burgeoning electric vehicle market, showcasing Nano One Materials as a key holding. UNWPX's focus on these materials led to a 70.60% return in 2020, significantly outperforming benchmark indices.

title: Was That the IPO Stocks Bubble that Just Popped?
summary: The Renaissance IPO ETF ($IPO) and ARK Innovation ETF ($ARKK) have both experienced significant drops from their recent highs, raising questions about whether the IPO stocks bubble has popped. The article highlights the extreme exuberance in these high-flying stocks, comparing it to the 1999 dot-com bubble, and suggests that changing sentiment in these areas could signal a broader wobble in the market.

title: Steer clear of Tesla, look at semiconductors, says American Century
summary: American Century Investments advises investors to avoid Tesla (TSLA) due to its high valuation and instead consider component suppliers for electric and autonomous vehicles, such as Aptiv (APTV), NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), and Cree (CREE). Brent Puff, a senior portfolio manager at American Century, highlights the significant growth potential in electrification and autonomous driving, suggesting these lesser-known semiconductor companies offer a better risk-reward profile than Tesla. Morningstar analysts largely agree on Tesla's overvaluation and competitive challenges, while noting some of the recommended companies are either fairly valued or, in Aptiv's case, overvalued despite strong fundamentals.

title: The Parent of All Parents: Here's What Berkshire Hathaway Actually Does
summary: Berkshire Hathaway is a holding company led by Warren Buffett that owns about 70 private companies and minority stakes in 41 public stocks across various sectors. While it doesn't engage in manufacturing, it controls company shares and investment interests. Buffett is the top shareholder, and notable holdings include significant stakes in Apple and Coca-Cola, with a clear disinterest in investing in Tesla.

title: 'Buzz' ETF tracking social media sentiment launches Thursday amid Reddit manias in stocks
summary: The Van Eck Vectors Social Sentiment ETF (BUZZ) has launched, aiming to track social media sentiment around stocks rather than price momentum. This ETF selects 75 stocks with bullish social media sentiment, based on a minimum $5 billion market cap and consistent social media mentions. While leveraging social media data, the ETF's criteria are designed to exclude the highly speculative "Reddit meme stocks" like GameStop, focusing instead on broader discussions.

title: Why Cathie Wood's once hot Ark Innovation ETF has lost all its 2021 gains
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK), which skyrocketed in 2020, has lost all its 2021 gains, declining 5.5% on Thursday and bringing its year-to-date decline to a similar amount. This pullback reflects a broader trend in tech stocks, driven by rising 10-year Treasury yields and fears of inflation leading to higher interest rates, which disproportionately affect growth stocks. The ETF's top holdings, including Tesla, Square, Roku, Teladoc, and Spotify, have seen significant declines.

title: BUZZ, the ETF of Social-Media Darlings, Drops in Trading Debut
summary: The VanEck Vectors Social Sentiment ETF (BUZZ) began trading, aiming to capitalize on the retail-investing trend and the influence of social media buzz on stock performance. This ETF includes stocks like Tesla and DraftKings, aiming to capture the "new era of investing" where information is sourced and shared online.

title: Volvo XC40 Recharge Relies on Analog Devices Battery Management System
summary: The Volvo XC40 Recharge, an all-electric crossover SUV, utilizes Analog Devices, Inc.'s battery management system (BMS) and integrated circuits to maximize its driving range and performance. The ADI system helps the vehicle meet its EPA-predicted 208-mile range and facilitates fast charging capabilities. Beyond battery management, ADI's Automotive Audio Bus (A2B) also contributes to the vehicle's design by reducing wiring weight, which further enhances range.

title: Four Investments of Nancy Pelosi and Her Husband Reveal Much
summary: The article discusses four significant investments made by House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and her husband, Paul Pelosi, on December 22. These investments include shares in AllianceBernstein (AB) and call options in Apple (AAPL), Tesla (TSLA), and Walt Disney Co (DIS), totaling between $1,751,003 and $3,500,000. Experts weigh in on the implications of these bullish trades, noting that while the Pelosis are wealthy, their investment choices align with market opportunities, although the full scope and reasoning behind the trades are not publicly known.

title: Tech-heavy Nasdaq hits correction with 10.5% fall from peak
summary: The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite has entered correction territory, falling 10.5% from its February peak, as technology shares experienced a significant sell-off. This downturn was driven by concerns over rising bond yields and inflation fears stemming from a new $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief bill. While financial, restaurant, and travel stocks rose on reopening hopes, they couldn't offset the weight of declining big tech shares like Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla.

title: Tesla to boost Texas energy grid with secret mega-battery, report says
summary: Tesla is reportedly building a 100-megawatt mega-battery in Angleton, Texas, through a subsidiary named Gambit Energy Storage LLC, to enter the state's power market. This project aims to support the Texas energy grid, which faced near-total collapse during recent winter storms. The battery's construction comes amid increased scrutiny of Texas's energy infrastructure and Tesla CEO Elon Musk's growing presence and investments in the state.

title: ARK ETFs Erase 2021 Gains, Assets Hold
summary: Three of ARK Invest's seven ETFs, including the flagship ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), have erased their 2021 gains as of early March, experiencing significant drops in value due to a sell-off in high-growth stocks. Despite these performance setbacks, all seven ARK ETFs have continued to register net inflows year-to-date, indicating persistent investor interest and confidence in the firm's disruptive technology themes. Assets under management for the ARK ETFs collectively reached $52.8 billion, making ARK the ninth-largest ETF issuer.

title: Steel Dynamics Inc. ranks No. 1 in Fortune metal industry list
summary: Steel Dynamics Inc. (SDI) was ranked No. 1 in the metals industry category on Fortune's World’s Most Admired Companies list. This recognition, based on a poll of corporate executives, directors, and analysts, highlights SDI's strong operational and financial performance, innovation, and leadership. The article also notes SDI's new plant in Sinton, Texas, is expected to be operational this year and may supply steel to Tesla's Gigafactory for the Cybertruck.

title: Tesla loses a third of its value for the third time in a year
summary: Tesla Inc.'s stock experienced its third significant drop in a year, losing a third of its value from its January record high, primarily due to investor concerns about rising interest rates affecting high-valuation stocks. The selloff wiped off nearly $300 billion from its market capitalization, moving it behind Facebook. This decline is more pronounced than other major tech companies, and its shares have steadily fallen since announcing a bitcoin purchase, even as bitcoin’s price climbed.

title: Tesla shares bounce back following steep five-day decline
summary: Tesla shares rebounded on Tuesday after experiencing a significant five-day decline, which erased about $149 billion from its valuation. The recovery was fueled by positive news, including an analyst upgrade from New Street Research, a rally in Bitcoin, and a general shift in sentiment towards high-multiple technology stocks. Analyst Pierre Ferragu upgraded Tesla to buy, citing strong earnings momentum and demand, suggesting the stock could trade at a high multiple similar to Amazon's historical performance.

title: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF surges more than 10% for its best day ever
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK) surged over 10% for its best day ever, driven by a rebound in tech stocks like Tesla, Zoom Video, and Palantir. This rally helped recoup some recent sharp losses for the fund, which had been impacted by a market rotation out of high-growth tech into value stocks. Despite recent volatility, Wood remains confident in her disruptive strategy, viewing the sell-off as an opportunity to buy.

title: Exclusive: LG hopes to make new battery cells for Tesla in 2023 in U.S. or Europe -sources
summary: LG Energy Solution aims to produce advanced 4680 battery cells for Tesla's electric vehicles by 2023, considering manufacturing sites in the United States and Europe. While LG has made samples, it faces technological hurdles and has not yet secured orders from Tesla for these new cells, which Tesla is also developing in-house. LG currently supplies smaller cells to Tesla in China and is a major battery supplier for other automotive giants like General Motors.

title: West Michigan gets first Tesla service center in Grand Rapids
summary: Tesla is opening its first service center in West Michigan, located in Grand Rapids, following a settlement with the state that allows the company to sell and service its vehicles directly to customers. This new facility, which will also handle sales and delivery, is part of Tesla's expansion after previously being restricted from direct sales and service in Michigan. Michigan residents previously had to travel out-of-state for Tesla purchases and service.

title: If You Invested $1,000 In Tesla 10 Years Ago, Here's How Much You'd Have Now
summary: This article evaluates the return on a hypothetical $1,000 investment in Tesla Motors (NASDAQ: TSLA) made 10 years ago. It highlights Tesla's growth from its IPO to becoming a major electric vehicle manufacturer, detailing its stock performance, market capitalization milestones, and recent fluctuations. The article illustrates the substantial profit an early investor would have accrued despite the stock's volatility.

title: BHP moves nickel and copper HQ to Toronto as Canada emerges as new clean-tech mining hotspot
summary: BHP Group Ltd. is relocating its nickel and copper exploration headquarters to Toronto, recognizing Canada as a growing hub for clean-tech mining due to anticipated surges in demand for these metals from the electric vehicle industry. Laura Tyler, BHP's chief technical officer, highlighted Toronto's strong position for mineral exploration and innovation, aligning with the company's strategy to expand its Canadian footprint through collaborations and potential deals with junior exploration firms. The move signifies a strategic shift by BHP to capitalize on the increasing global demand for battery metals driven by the transition to a low-carbon economy.

title: Gaming platform Roblox’s stock gains after Cathie Wood buys in
summary: Shares of gaming platform Roblox Corp jumped on Thursday after its stock market debut, buoyed by Cathie Wood's ARK Next Generation Internet exchange traded fund buying more than 500,000 shares. The purchase weighted Roblox at 0.47 percent of the fund and added to the strongest opening ever for a direct stock market listing. The company's stock rose 5.3 percent in late morning trades, having been up more than 20 percent earlier in the day.

title: Promotion? Musk is ‘Technoking of Tesla’, CFO is ‘Master of Coin’
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has adopted the new title "Technoking of Tesla," and CFO Zach Kirkhorn is now "Master of Coin," according to a regulatory filing, though both retain their original executive titles. Additionally, Jerome Guillen, previously president of automotive, has transitioned to lead Tesla's heavy trucking program, a move analysts view positively as the company prepares to enter the critical heavy-trucks market.

title: DMS disrupted? Not just 2 giants now
summary: The article discusses the disruption in the Dealer Management System (DMS) market, traditionally dominated by CDK and Reynolds and Reynolds. New challengers like Tekion are emerging, with clients expressing satisfaction with their offerings. The piece suggests a shift in the competitive landscape of the DMS sector.

title: Tesla Names Jerome Guillen President of Heavy Trucking
summary: Tesla has appointed Jerome Guillen as president of its heavy trucking division, signaling a strategic focus on the electric Semi program. Guillen, formerly president of automotive, will now lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi, including charging and servicing networks, as the company plans to start deliveries by the end of 2021. This move has been viewed positively by investors, with analysts highlighting Tesla's commitment to its trucking vision.

title: ElectraMeccanica picks Mesa as site of new Arizona factory to build unusual electric cars
summary: ElectraMeccanica Vehicles Corp. has chosen Mesa, Arizona, as the location for its new assembly and engineering center, which will build its three-wheeled, single-seat SOLO electric cars. The facility is expected to create between 200 and 500 jobs and could produce up to 20,000 vehicles annually. Arizona offered a compelling incentive package and a strong workforce, making it the preferred choice over Tennessee.

title: Volkswagen aims to knock Tesla out of top spot by 2025 in major EV push
summary: Volkswagen plans to become the global electric vehicle market leader by 2025, surpassing Tesla, by increasing cost-saving efforts, standardizing technologies, and boosting EV sales to 1 million this year. The company will focus on a "platform" approach for economies of scale, expand its software division to compete with tech giants, and aims for an operating return on sales of 7% to 8% by 2025. This aggressive strategy includes significant investments in battery production and software development despite challenges posed by the pandemic and semiconductor shortages.

title: CleanSpark: Ignore the Noise and Buy the Stock in 2021
summary: CleanSpark (CLSK) stock opened significantly lower after announcing a discounted stock sale. Despite this, analysts are bullish on CLSK, with a median target price suggesting over 100% upside. CleanSpark is positioned as a dual bet on bitcoin mining and microgrids, with strong revenue growth and attractive margins across its business segments.

title: Classic Range Rover Electromod Is Powered By A Tesla Drivetrain And Can Hit 60MPH In 5.2 Sec
summary: E.C.D. Automotive Design has completed its first electric conversion, transforming a Classic Range Rover into an electromod powered by a Tesla drivetrain. This restomod can achieve 0-60 mph in 5.2 seconds and boasts a 220-mile range from its 100 kWh battery pack. The company plans to continue electrifying other Land Rovers following this successful project.

title: Which Is a Better Buy? BLNK Versus CHPT Stock
summary: This article evaluates Blink Charging (BLNK) and ChargePoint (CHPT) stock to determine which is a better investment in the rapidly growing EV-charging sector. It compares their market share, valuation multiples, and growth prospects, highlighting ChargePoint's larger footprint and more favorable valuation despite the increased competition in the space. The author concludes that ChargePoint is a better bet due to its leadership position and lower valuation.

title: KULR Partners with Andretti for EV Thermal Tech
summary: KULR Technology Group announced a long-term partnership with Andretti Technologies to bring space-proven thermal management technology from Mars Rover missions to EV motorsports. The collaboration aims to develop high-performance battery solutions with top safety ratings for racing and eventually transfer this technology to mass-market EV applications. The partnership emphasizes sustainable battery management systems and preventing thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries.

title: Leverage Shares launches 25 single stock short and leveraged ETPs
summary: Leverage Shares has introduced 25 new single-stock short and leveraged (S&L) Exchange-Traded Products (ETPs) on the London Stock Exchange, expanding its existing range. These ETPs track STOXX indices and include prominent names like Tesla and PayPal, as well as UK blue chips such as Barclays and BP. The products are physically backed and available in USD, GBP, and EUR, catering to investors looking to capitalize on market shifts and hedge exposures in volatile markets.

title: EV Makers Fall on Lordstown SEC Review, Nikola Investor Sale
summary: Electric-vehicle (EV) startups experienced a downturn due to issues at Lordstown Motors and Nikola, compounded by rising Treasury yields. Lordstown Motors (RIDE), Nikola Corp. (NKLA), Nio Inc. (NIO), Workhorse Group Inc. (WKHS), XPeng Inc. (XPEV), and Li Auto Inc. (LI) all saw declines. Tesla Inc. (TSLA) also fell after the UK reduced its purchasing bonus for EVs, disqualifying Tesla models from subsidies.

title: What Happens When You Smash a Tesla Into a Vintage Range Rover?
summary: E.C.D. Automotive Design, a restomodding company based in Florida, is building electric Range Rover Classics using Tesla drivetrains. These modified vehicles aim to resolve the notorious unreliability of vintage Land Rovers while offering a modern electric power source and extended range. The custom-built electric Range Rovers start at around $195,000, with higher-end builds approaching $300,000.

title: New Meets Old in This Tesla-Powered Range Rover Classic
summary: East Coast Defenders (E.C.D.) Automotive Design has introduced an electric conversion for Range Rover Classics, featuring a Tesla Direct Drive EV powertrain and 100-kWh battery pack. This allows the classic SUV to achieve 0-60 mph in 5.2 seconds and offers a 220-mile range. The vehicle retains its vintage exterior while boasting a luxurious, modern interior, highlighting a growing trend of electrifying classic cars.

title: The Solid-State Race: Legacy Automakers Reach for Battery Breakthrough
summary: Legacy automakers are actively pursuing solid-state battery technology through partnerships with startups to gain an advantage in the electric vehicle (EV) market. This technology promises enhanced energy density, longer range, and faster charging compared to current lithium-ion batteries. While companies like Volkswagen and GM are deeply invested in this race, Tesla is notably absent, indicating its confidence in evolving existing battery designs.

title: Musk says Tesla would be shut down if its cars spied in China, elsewhere
summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla, stated that his company would be shut down if its vehicles were discovered to be spying in China or anywhere else, in response to reports that China's military had banned Teslas from its facilities due to security concerns over in-car cameras. Speaking at a prominent Chinese forum, Musk emphasized the strong incentive for the company to maintain confidentiality. This development comes as Tesla faces increasing competition in China, its second-largest market.

title: How Texas is luring big businesses and billionaires away from California
summary: Texas is experiencing a significant economic boom, attracting numerous companies and wealthy individuals from California, including major tech firms like Oracle, Tesla, and Apple. This migration is fueled by factors prompting a "tremendous increase" in relocations and expansions, making Texas a burgeoning business hub. The article explores the reasons behind this trend and its potential implications for the state's future.

title: 3 Mid-Cap Global Battery Manufacturer Stocks
summary: This article examines three mid-cap global battery manufacturers: Varta AG (Germany), EnerSys (USA), and Simplo Technology (Taiwan), as potential investment opportunities given the growing demand for lithium-ion batteries. It details each company's business model, revenue streams, and market position, highlighting both their strengths and potential risks. The piece concludes by suggesting that foreign battery stocks can offer diversification for investors looking beyond domestic options.

title: EV Startups Blocked From Market by Dealerships and an Old Legal Structure
summary: EV startups like Rivian, Lucid, and Lordstown are challenging existing state laws in the U.S. that largely prohibit direct-to-consumer vehicle sales, a system maintained by established auto dealerships. These startups, along with Tesla, advocate for coexisting sales models, arguing that the traditional dealership structure is ill-suited for the nascent EV market and impedes consumer adoption. Dealership associations, however, contend that current laws protect consumers and promote competition, while legacy automakers are exploring ways to integrate online sales with their franchise models.

title: Lucid Motors Deepens Expertise with Executive Team Additions and Promotions
summary: Lucid Motors has strengthened its executive team with significant additions and promotions as it prepares for customer deliveries of its Lucid Air EV in the second half of 2021. The company appointed Michael Bell as Senior VP of Digital, Achim Pantfoerder as VP of Program Management, and Nicolas Minbiole as VP of Global Quality. Additionally, Eric Bach was promoted to Senior VP – Product and Chief Engineer, and Derek Jenkins to Senior VP – Design and Brand, demonstrating Lucid's commitment to quality and innovation.

title: Frito-Lay Replaces All Diesel Vehicles at Facility With Cleaner Tech
summary: Frito-Lay has transitioned its Modesto, California snack food facility to nearly eliminate diesel vehicles by adopting zero-emission and near-zero-emission technologies. This initiative, part of PepsiCo's broader goal to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by over 40% by 2030, includes electric forklifts, yard trucks, box trucks, and CNG tractors, with Tesla Semi rigs expected later in the year. The company estimates this shift has already cut greenhouse gas pollution by 53% and serves as a prototype for scaling sustainable supply chain operations.

title: Tesla Cybertruck, Semi timing crucial for stock to avoid sell-off: Piper Sandler
summary: Piper Sandler analysts Alexander Potter and Winnie Dong suggest that Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) faces a potential investor sell-off if the production timelines for the Cybertruck and Semi are not clarified soon.
