The move comes as regulations, such as California's planned ban on new gasoline-powered vehicle sales by 2035, accelerate the transition to electric vehicles.

title: Uranium Stocks Soar As Elon Musk Applauds the Alternative Energy Source
summary: Uranium stocks are rising amidst increasing global interest in nuclear power as an alternative energy source. This interest is driven by the ongoing global energy crisis and the war in Ukraine. Elon Musk has voiced his approval for the return to nuclear energy and highlighted the need for fossil fuels in the short term to maintain civilization.

title: Hyundai narrows Level 3 self-driving tech gap with Tesla to one year
summary: Hyundai Motor Co. has significantly narrowed its Level 3 self-driving technology gap with Tesla to just one year, with plans to launch Level 3 cars starting with the Genesis G90 later this year. The company aims to surpass Tesla in system computation speeds within a few years and intends to roll out fully autonomous vehicles by 2030. Hyundai also revealed it has cross-checked its technology by disassembling a Tesla Model 3 and plans to reduce integrated controllers in future IONIQ models for better efficiency.

title: U.S. agency: 'unlawful' for Tesla to prevent employees from wearing union shirts
summary: The National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) ruled that it was unlawful for Tesla Inc. to prohibit employees from wearing shirts with union insignia, reaffirming the right to display union clothing. This decision stems from a 2017 dispute with the United Automobile Workers (UAW) union and reverses a prior 2019 NLRB ruling involving Walmart Inc. The NLRB ordered Tesla to rescind its policy against union shirts, noting this is not the first clash between Tesla and the agency.

title: Honda Motor, LG Energy to build $4.4 bln U.S. EV battery plant
summary: Honda Motor and LG Energy Solution announced a joint venture to build a $4.4 billion lithium-ion battery plant for electric vehicles in the U.S., with a target annual production capacity of 40 GWh. The batteries will exclusively supply Honda facilities in North America for Honda and Acura EV models, with construction planned for early 2023 and mass production by the end of 2025. This move aligns with U.S. government policies pushing for domestic battery and EV manufacturing and comes as the country implements stricter regulations and tax credit eligibility for EVs.

title: Which Charging Networks Can your EV Access?
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to electric vehicle (EV) charging networks in the U.S., detailing which networks are compatible with various 2022 and 2023 EV models. It explains that most EVs use standard Level 2 and DC fast-charging connectors, with exceptions like Tesla's Supercharger and Rivian's Adventure Network. The article also lists incentives offered by automakers for specific charging networks.

title: 10 features from the ’80s and ’90s that either hit hard or missed big
summary: This article looks back at ten automotive innovations from the 1980s and 1990s, categorizing them as either a "hit" or a "miss." It examines features like four-wheel steering, digital dashboards, pop-up headlamps, keyless entry, electronic stability control, and satellite navigation, discussing their initial reception and long-term impact on car design and technology. The author highlights how some ideas were ahead of their time, while others were flawed in execution or eventually replaced by better solutions.

title: Lincoln Electric Launches a DC Fast Charge EV Charger Initiative
summary: Lincoln Electric Holdings has announced a new initiative to design and manufacture DC fast charge electric vehicle (EV) chargers for the U.S. market. The company has developed a scalable 50kW DC fast charger power module, with plans for a production model in 2023, leveraging its Cleveland, Ohio, facility. This move aims to address "range anxiety" and accelerate EV adoption by providing reliable and durable fast-charging infrastructure.

title: The electric vehicle boom could bring lithium mines back to North Carolina
summary: Driven by the electric vehicle boom and the Inflation Reduction Act, lithium mining companies are looking to reopen mines in North Carolina, a region with significant lithium deposits and a history of mining. However, these plans face strong opposition from local residents concerned about environmental impacts like water contamination, dust, and increased traffic. While some communities in North Carolina are supportive of the mining developments due to potential economic benefits, others highlight the contentious trade-offs between clean energy goals and localized environmental and social costs of mineral extraction.

title: Portable Charging Solutions for EVs
summary: Running out of power in an EV can leave drivers stranded, as nationwide roadside EV charging services are not yet widely available. While towing to a nearby charging station is the most common solution, several companies offer portable charging devices like SparkCharge's Roadie, Blink's Mobile Emergency Charger, and FreeWire Technologies' Mobi EV Charger, primarily targeting commercial customers and roadside assistance providers. AAA, which once offered a limited EV charging trial, now opts for towing, noting that EV drivers are generally much more range-aware than gasoline vehicle drivers.

title: Gatik, Pitney Bowes Team on Driverless Trucks
summary: Gatik, a California-based autonomous truck technology company, has partnered with Pitney Bowes to integrate its Class 6 autonomous box trucks into Pitney Bowes' e-commerce logistics network. Starting in the first quarter of next year, Gatik's self-driving fleet will operate a continuous loop in Dallas, aiming to enhance delivery speed, efficiency, and potentially reduce transportation costs for Pitney Bowes. This collaboration highlights Gatik's focus on middle-mile logistics and its strategy of using smaller autonomous trucks for frequent, short-haul routes.

title: POSCO builds EV battery recycling plant in Poland
summary: POSCO Holdings has completed the construction of PLSC, a secondary battery recycling plant in Brzeg Dolny, Poland, in partnership with SungEel HiTech. The plant has an annual production capacity of 7,000 tons of black mass, which will be used to extract critical battery materials like lithium, nickel, cobalt, and manganese. This initiative is part of POSCO Group's broader strategy to establish a stable secondary material value chain and achieve significant sales in the sector by 2030, reinforcing their commitment to ESG management and circular economy principles.

title: Cruise lines to begin using Elon Musk's Starlink Wi-Fi
summary: Royal Caribbean Group, including brands Royal Caribbean, Celebrity Cruises, and Silversea Cruises, will implement Elon Musk's Starlink Wi-Fi across its fleet by the end of Q1 2023. This initiative aims to provide significantly faster and more reliable internet connectivity for both passengers and crew, addressing the long-standing issue of slow and expensive internet at sea. The cost structure for Starlink will vary by brand, with Silversea offering it free, Celebrity including basic Wi-Fi with premium upgrade options, and Royal Caribbean yet to announce its pricing model.

title: Formerly Sacred Now Rotting Silicon Valley Dictum of “Growth at All Costs” Crushes Okta: Shares Collapse 80% from Peak
summary: Okta, a company that provides secure access to cloud-based systems, has seen its shares collapse by 80% from their February 2021 peak after reporting a $210 million net loss and lowering its guidance. Despite consistent and growing annual net losses exceeding $2 billion, executives and analysts have ironically reframed these as "profitability," highlighting a prevailing Silicon Valley mantra of "growth at all costs." The company's struggles are attributed to "sales challenges" and "integration challenges" related to its 2021 acquisition of Auth0, signaling the potential end of an era for this business model.

title: With Tesla Decision, NLRB Rules Dress Codes Unlawful That Restrict Pro-Union Apparel
summary: The NLRB has ruled in the Tesla Inc. case that workplace dress codes prohibiting pro-union apparel are presumptively unlawful, overturning a previous standard. Employers must now demonstrate "special circumstances" to justify such restrictions, with the NLRB rejecting Tesla's arguments regarding damage to vehicles. This decision signals a more pro-labor stance from the current NLRB and requires employers to review and potentially revise their dress code policies.

title: General Motors CEO reveals new electric vehicle
summary: General Motors CEO Mary Barra announced a new all-electric Chevrolet Equinox, priced around $30,000, aiming to make EVs more affordable and increase GM's electric product line to 40% by 2025. Barra also addressed supply chain challenges and the company's commitment to environmental goals.

title: Musk says SpaceX discussed iPhone satellite service with Apple
summary: Elon Musk revealed that SpaceX has engaged in discussions with Apple Inc. regarding the integration of Starlink's satellite connectivity into iPhones. This announcement follows Apple's recent partnership with Globalstar Inc. for satellite services on its latest iPhone model, indicating a growing trend in offering satellite-based communication for smartphones. Musk emphasized that dedicated technology is crucial for optimal satellite-to-cell phone service.

title: Meme stocks to watch: top trending Reddit shares in September 2022
summary: This article identifies the top ten trending meme stocks on Reddit for September 2022, explaining what meme stocks are and their inherent benefits and risks, primarily high volatility. It then provides a detailed look into each of the ten companies, including their recent stock performance, significant events, and relevant analyst commentary, noting that all data is from a 30-day period prior to September 8, 2022.

title: TESLA Inc. looking to bring lithium refinery to Coastal Bend
summary: Tesla Inc. is considering building a "battery-grade lithium hydroxide refining facility" in the Coastal Bend area of Texas, near Robstown, or potentially in Louisiana. The company has applied for tax breaks from the state of Texas, which could lead to significant job creation and economic growth for the chosen location. However, the proposal faces concerns regarding water usage and environmental impact from some local residents.

title: Lucid Group Is Now Reportedly Manufacturing 40 to 50 Cars per Day After a Broad-based Logistics Overhaul and Management Reshuffle
summary: Lucid Group has reportedly increased its daily car production to 40-50 units following significant logistics overhauls and management changes. This improvement comes after repeated downward revisions of its 2022 production targets, which were initially over 20,000 units but later dropped to 6,000-7,000 units. The company aims to meet its revised annual guidance by further increasing production and benefiting from a new Saudi Arabian facility and purchase agreement.

title: The New Vision of General Motors: Zero Accidents, Zero Emissions and Zero Congestion
summary: General Motors is shifting its focus to a new vision centered on zero accidents, zero emissions, and zero congestion, driven by electromobility and technological development. This transformation involves connecting vehicles, developing solutions for diverse consumer needs, and pioneering new technologies like the Ultium battery platform and autonomous driving. The company emphasizes its readiness to lead the change towards a sustainable future in mobility.

title: Under the Hood of RCD
summary: The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF (RCD) saw significant inflows in August, making it the most popular Invesco equal-weight sector ETF for the month. RCD offers investors exposure to the consumer discretionary sector with an equal-weighted approach, diversifying away from large-cap bias and providing a tilt towards smaller, potentially undervalued companies. This strategy aims to reduce concentration risk by ensuring each of its 60 holdings, including companies like Etsy, Tesla, and Amazon, receives approximately equal allocation during quarterly rebalances.

title: The best ways to buy strategic metals
summary: This article discusses investment opportunities in strategic metals, particularly in the alternative-energy sector, despite recent price weaknesses. The author highlights companies and ETFs related to battery technology and nuclear energy, explaining that short-term price fluctuations may obscure long-term structural drivers like increased demand for EVs and the need for new mining and refining capacity. Investors are advised to consider these niches as a potential opportunity if they believe in a structural transformation away from hydrocarbons.

title: Auto parts supplier Aptiv to acquire 85% of Intercable unit in EV tech push
summary: Aptiv Plc announced its acquisition of an 85% stake in Intercable Automotive Solutions for 595 million euros. This strategic move grants Aptiv access to high-voltage busbar technology crucial for electric vehicles and aligns with its broader investments in EV and battery technology. The deal, expected to close by the end of the year, aims to bolster Aptiv's earnings next year and diversify its revenue stream.

title: Tesla wants to mine Lithium in Nigeria: What are the hidden costs?
summary: Nigeria rejected Tesla's request to mine lithium unless the company establishes a battery-making factory within the West African nation to add value to the mineral. The Nigerian minister of mines is seeking other lithium miners who align with the country's industrial policy. This decision aligns with Nigeria's goal of retaining value along the global processing chain of lithium, a mineral whose demand is projected to triple by 2040.

title: South Star Battery Metals announces test drilling at Alabama graphite project
summary: South Star Battery Metals is commencing test drilling this month at its Ceylon Graphite Project in Coosa County, Alabama, to assess the extent of mineralization. The project is strategically located in the Alabama Graphite Belt, an area significant for rare earth minerals essential for EV batteries. This initiative aims to generate data for a preliminary economic assessment by late 2023, bolstering U.S. critical minerals supply in a market currently dominated by China.

title: Palo Alto Networks 3-for-1 stock split: What to Know
summary: Palo Alto Networks completed a 3-for-1 stock split, with shares gaining slightly on the first day of trading post-split before moving into negative territory. Shareholders of record as of September 6 received two additional shares for each one held, distributed after the close of trading on September 13. The company stated the split aims to make shares more accessible to employees and a broader base of investors, following significant stock price increases since its IPO.

title: PANW Stock Falls After Palo Alto Stock Split. What to Know.
summary: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock experienced a slight decline despite a 3-for-1 stock split on September 14, 2022. This performance was unexpected by some investors given a broader market rebound and the company's strong financial results and outlook. While stock splits don't add inherent value, studies suggest they can benefit stock prices over a 12-month period.

title: Tesla struggles with Elon Musk’s strict return-to-office policy
summary: Three months after Elon Musk's strict return-to-office mandate, Tesla faces challenges with insufficient office space and resources to accommodate all employees. The policy has led to a decline in morale, increased absenteeism tracking, and the dismissal of some remote workers who could not relocate, impacting the company's ability to retain talent.

title: Tesla (TSLA) Keeps Duping Consumers About Self-Driving Cars, Suit Says
summary: Tesla Inc. is facing a class-action lawsuit for allegedly misleading consumers about the capabilities of its self-driving cars. A California man claims the company deceptively marketed its driver-assistance systems, continuously promising advancements that have not materialized. This suit follows similar accusations from California's Department of Motor Vehicles regarding false advertising.

title: Tesla is sued by drivers over alleged false Autopilot, Full Self-Driving claims
summary: Tesla is facing a proposed class-action lawsuit from drivers who allege that the company and Elon Musk falsely advertised its Autopilot and Full Self-Driving features. The lawsuit claims Tesla misled the public into believing these technologies were fully functional or imminent since 2016, despite known deficiencies, to boost sales and stock price. This legal action follows similar complaints from California's Department of Motor Vehicles regarding the overstatement of Tesla's advanced driver assistance systems.

title: NIU zooms into Brickell with new flagship store
summary: NIU, a Beijing-based and Nasdaq-traded company, has opened a new flagship store in Brickell, Miami, expanding its South Florida presence. The company sells electric-powered mobility devices like kick scooters, ebikes, and mopeds, aiming to offer sustainable and efficient transportation options. NIU's head of North America, Benjamin McGill, stated that the store's location in Brickell is strategic for building brand presence in the US and challenging the perception that alternative mobility solutions don't fit American transportation needs.

title: Chevron is starting to talk to retail investors in a brand new way
summary: Chevron is engaging with retail investors for the first time through a digital Q&A, signaling a broader trend where traditional companies like U.S. Steel and Howard Hughes Corporation are also increasing outreach to individual shareholders. This shift is driven by new digital communication platforms that make it easier and more cost-effective to identify and engage a growing and highly engaged retail investor base. These platforms enable discussions on broader business issues like ESG, company culture, and long-term strategy, demonstrating that retail investors are more informed and seek meaningful engagement beyond quarterly earnings.

title: Asset Allocation, International Stocks, Bonds, and Small and Mid Cap Value Factors
summary: This article discusses various aspects of asset allocation, including whether it should change in retirement, the rationale for international stock investing despite recent US outperformance, and concerns about bonds in a bear market. It also covers the pros and cons of small-cap vs. mid-cap value funds, considerations for taxable accounts, and the balance between saving and spending money after achieving financial independence.

title: TSLQ Stock Fund Price and Chart — NASDAQ:TSLQ
summary: This article provides detailed information on the Tradr 2X Short TSLA Daily ETF (TSLQ), including its current price, chart data, key statistics like AUM and expense ratio, and its investment strategy. It highlights that TSLQ is a short-term tactical tool designed to deliver -2x the daily price return of Tesla stock and discusses its recent name changes and risks. The article also includes various trading ideas and technical analyses from different contributors regarding TSLQ.

title: Off to the (24) races: F1 is capitalizing on its growing audience
summary: Formula 1 announced a record-breaking 24-race calendar for 2023, showcasing its growing global audience, particularly in the US. This expansion follows Liberty Media's acquisition in 2017 and strategic moves like the Netflix series "Drive To Survive," which significantly boosted viewership and interest. The new schedule includes an inaugural Las Vegas Grand Prix, marking a substantial push into the American market.

title: How much does it really cost to charge an electric vehicle?
summary: This article provides a cost comparison between charging an electric vehicle and fueling a gasoline-powered car, focusing on Entergy's service area. It calculates the daily cost of charging an EV at home, considers the investment in Level 2 home chargers, and discusses public charging options. The analysis concludes that electric vehicles offer significant fuel cost savings and overall ownership benefits over time.

title: Ford stock sinks on inflation, supply constraints warning
summary: Ford Motor Co.'s stock dropped 12% after the automaker warned that inflation and supply constraints would negatively impact its third-quarter earnings, leading to a projected $1 billion increase in supplier costs. Ford expects Q3 adjusted earnings before interest and taxes to be significantly lower than previous quarters, ranging from $1.4 billion to $1.7 billion, and anticipates 40,000 to 45,000 vehicles will be assembled but awaiting parts. Despite these issues, Ford reaffirmed its full-year guidance, while analysts expressed concerns about management's handling of the situation and the slow recovery from supply chain problems.

title: GM to sell up to 175,000 electric vehicles to Hertz through 2027
summary: General Motors has agreed to sell up to 175,000 electric vehicles to Hertz Global over the next five years, starting early next year with Chevy Bolt EV and EUV models. This deal is GM's largest vehicle sale agreement with Hertz, following similar agreements between Hertz and Tesla and Polestar, and aims to significantly increase EV adoption and Hertz's electric fleet. Despite a broader market decline, the companies decided not to release financial details of the deal, but GM plans to sell the EVs at "retail margin" rather than at discounted fleet sales.

title: 7 Things to Know About the NANC ETF Aiming to Track Nancy Pelosi Stocks
summary: Unusual Whales has proposed two new ETFs, NANC and KRUZ, designed to track the trading activities of Democratic and Republican lawmakers, respectively. The NANC ETF is inspired by Speaker Nancy Pelosi's successful trades, while KRUZ would follow Republican activity, including Senator Ted Cruz. These ETFs aim to allow investors to mirror the investment decisions of politicians, leveraging their perceived stock-picking skills.

title: NVIDIA Unveils DRIVE Thor — Centralized Car Computer Unifying Cluster, Infotainment, Automated Driving, and Parking in a Single, Cost-Saving System
summary: NVIDIA announced DRIVE Thor, its next-generation centralized computer for autonomous vehicles, delivering up to 2,000 teraflops of performance. This superchip unifies intelligent functions like automated driving, parking, and infotainment into a single architecture, significantly reducing system cost and complexity. ZEEKR, a Geely-owned automaker, is the first customer, planning to integrate DRIVE Thor into its intelligent electric vehicles starting in early 2025.

title: GM backs setting tough U.S. emissions targets for 2030
summary: General Motors (GM) announced its support for stricter federal emissions standards, aiming for at least 50% of new vehicles sold by 2030 to be zero-emission. This stance, articulated with the Environmental Defense Fund (EDF), comes as the EPA develops new requirements and aligns with GM's goal to eliminate tailpipe emissions from new light-duty vehicles by 2035. The move also highlights ongoing discussions and differing approaches between the federal government, California, and various environmental groups regarding the pace and scope of EV adoption.

title: China's Xpeng says CATL is no longer its largest battery supplier
summary: Xpeng, a Chinese electric car maker, has diversified its battery suppliers and no longer considers CATL its largest. This move reflects a broader trend among Chinese EV automakers to seek alternative suppliers to better control costs, especially after CATL raised prices. Xpeng is now working with multiple battery makers, including Sunwoda for fast-charging technology and EVE and CALB for its vehicles.

title: 7 Meme Stocks to Buy During a Stock Market Crash
summary: This article identifies seven meme stocks that aggressive investors might consider buying during a stock market crash for long-term potential. The selection includes companies like Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), FedEx (FDX), GameStop (GME), NVIDIA (NVDA), Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT), and Tesla (TSLA). Each stock is discussed with reasons for its meme stock appeal and potential for recovery despite current market downturns.

title: SolarEdge Home Battery Review: 3 Months In
summary: The author reviews his new SolarEdge Home Battery after three months of use, detailing the installation process, initial impressions, and challenges encountered. He highlights the benefits of the battery, including a free inverter upgrade and compatibility with Amber Electric's "SmartShift" for increased savings, despite minor issues like a 3-second switchover delay during outages and initial battery failure. The article also addresses common user questions and concerns regarding battery management and performance.

title: XPeng Diversifies Battery Sources, Reducing Reliance on CATL
summary: XPeng Inc. is diversifying its battery suppliers, reducing its primary reliance on CATL. The electric-vehicle maker has added Sunwoda Electronic Co. Ltd., CALB Co. Ltd., and Eve Energy Co. Ltd. to its supplier list, partly to better control costs after CATL raised prices. XPeng is also collaborating with Sunwoda to develop a fast-charging battery for its G9 SUV.

title: Weekly Recalls: Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz (2), Nissan (2), Tesla
summary: This article details the weekly vehicle recalls issued for Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz (two separate recalls), Nissan (two separate recalls), and Tesla. The recalls address issues ranging from fuel system defects and improperly tightened lug nuts to electrical system faults, detaching window trim, transmission park pawl problems, faulty seat belts, and malfunctioning automatic window reversal systems. Each recall specifies the affected models, potential number of units, the nature of the defect, the manufacturer's proposed remedy, and owner notification timelines.

title: Tesla Recalls Almost 1.1 Million Vehicles Over Window Glitch
summary: Tesla has recalled nearly 1.1 million vehicles across all four of its models due to a power window glitch where windows may close too quickly, posing a pinching risk to occupants. The electric car manufacturer plans to resolve this issue with an over-the-air software update, eliminating the need for vehicle owners to bring their cars in for service. The recall impacts Model S, X, 3, and Y vehicles manufactured between 2017 and 2022.

title: Hertz is buying up to 175,000 electric vehicles from GM
summary: Hertz has announced a major purchase of up to 175,000 electric vehicles from General Motors over the next five years, expanding its EV rental fleet. This follows earlier agreements with Tesla and Polestar. The acquisitions will include a variety of GM's North American passenger vehicle brands and types, with GM aiming to significantly ramp up EV production and Hertz targeting a quarter of its fleet to be electric by 2024.

title: GM Is Doubling Down on Self-Driving Cars With LiDAR
summary: General Motors is heavily investing in LiDAR technology for self-driving cars, catching the attention of institutional investors like Cathie Wood's ARK Invest. GM plans to pour $35 billion into EV and AV product development by 2025, with LiDAR being a crucial component for autonomous vehicles to navigate. The global LiDAR market is projected for significant growth, offering investment opportunities through ETFs and specialized tech stock services.

title: GM, Hertz make deal to deploy up to 175,000 EVs
summary: Hertz plans to purchase up to 175,000 electric vehicles from General Motors over the next five years, marking a substantial step towards Hertz's goal of having a quarter of its fleet be electric by the end of 2024. This multi-billion dollar deal could pave the way for similar partnerships between GM and other rental car companies, helping GM achieve its target of producing 1 million EVs annually in North America by 2025. The agreement allows GM to sell EVs at near-retail profit margins to Hertz, deploying them in key cities and helping to reduce carbon emissions.

title: How Hertz and the EV could remake your car rental
summary: Hertz and BP are collaborating to transform the car rental experience with electric vehicles, including building charging infrastructure and exploring services for ride-hailing drivers. Hertz plans for a quarter of its U.S. fleet to be electric by 2024, aiming to address the unique challenges of EV charging at scale and potentially using its facilities to serve other EV users. The move is driven by the financial imperative of maintaining residual car values and could introduce many Americans to EVs for the first time.

title: Hertz, bp collaborate to accelerate EV charging in North America
summary: Hertz and bp have signed a memorandum of understanding to develop a national network of EV charging stations in North America, powered by bp pulse. This partnership aims to accelerate EV consumer adoption by establishing fast-charging hubs at Hertz locations, managing Hertz's charging infrastructure, and customizing bp pulse's Omega software for efficient fleet recharging. Hertz plans for one-quarter of its fleet to be electric by the end of 2024, expanding charging options for customers and supporting lower-emission travel.

title: NIO unlocks its potential through standout user operations
summary: This article features an interview with Lihong Qin, cofounder and president of NIO, discussing the company's unique user-centric operating model for electric vehicles. Qin explains the business logic behind user operations, its role in creating a brand premium, and how it unlocks value throughout the vehicle lifecycle. The interview also touches on the economics of user operations, including optimizing sales and service costs, and NIO's expansion into European markets.

title: Pony.ai and SAIC AI Lab to Develop Fully Driverless EV Robotaxi
summary: Pony.ai and SAIC AI Lab have partnered to develop a fully driverless EV robotaxi, based on the SAIC Marvel R model, equipped with Pony.ai's L4-level autonomous driving technology. This collaboration will focus on co-developing vehicle chassis, intelligent cockpits, and remote assistance, aiming to accelerate the commercial adoption of robotaxi services in numerous Chinese cities. The initiative aligns with Shanghai's driverless policy and builds upon Pony.ai's expanding robotaxi services in the region.

title: Qualcomm CFO Focuses on Investing in Budding Automotive Business
summary: Qualcomm's CFO, Akash Palkhiwala, is strategically allocating investments towards the company's expanding automotive-chip business. This move is a diversification strategy to offset slowing consumer demand for smartphones, which traditionally has been a significant revenue driver for the company. Qualcomm, primarily known for mobile-phone chips, has secured $30 billion in commitments from auto-component suppliers to support this growth.

title: How China Is Transforming the Global Lithium Industry
summary: China has become a dominant force in the global lithium industry, controlling around 80% of battery cell manufacturing and holding key positions in both upstream and downstream supply chains. This ascendancy is driven by robust policy support, entrepreneurial breakthroughs from companies like CATL and BYD, and significant investments in lithium mines and energy storage solutions. China's strategic initiatives, including a shift towards LFP batteries and ambitious energy storage targets, position it to continue leading the lithium sector for the foreseeable future, impacting global renewable energy goals and EV adoption.

title: Tesla workers' lawsuit over layoffs likely belongs in arbitration, judge says
summary: A U.S. magistrate judge has recommended that a proposed class-action lawsuit against Tesla Inc, concerning alleged failures to provide advance notice for layoffs, be moved to private arbitration. The judge stated that an arbitrator, not a court, should determine the validity of the arbitration agreements signed by Tesla workers. This decision means former employees will likely pursue their claims individually in arbitration rather than through a class action.

title: Tesla names Airbnb co-founder to board
summary: Tesla Inc. has appointed Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia to its board of directors, bringing the total number of directors back to eight. Gebbia steps into a role previously held by Larry Ellison and continues to serve on Airbnb's board. He had previously stepped back from a daily operational role at Airbnb, which he co-founded in 2007.

title: Elon Musk seeks to end SEC 'muzzle' requiring pre-approval of tweets
summary: Elon Musk's lawyers have petitioned a federal appeals court to dismantle a provision within his 2018 consent decree with the SEC, which necessitates a Tesla lawyer's pre-approval for some of his tweets. They argue this requirement acts as a "government-imposed muzzle" violating free speech principles. The SEC has not yet commented but is expected to file its own brief in response.

title: Ford Rolls Out Gas-Guzzlers To Fund Its Green Energy Ambitions
summary: Ford Motor Co. is releasing new gas-guzzling pickup trucks, including its Super Duty series with powerful engines, to fund its ambitious green energy goals. Despite aiming for carbon neutrality by 2035 and investing $50 billion in electric vehicles, Ford relies heavily on the profitability of its F-series trucks, which generate nearly a third of its global revenues. This strategy highlights the trade-offs companies and even nations, like the E.U., must make during the transition to a greener economy, acknowledging that progress cannot happen overnight and requires sustained business operations.

title: ARK Invest CEO Cathie Wood’s tech bargain hunt
summary: Cathie Wood's ARK Invest continued its strategy of investing in tech stocks in September 2022, acquiring shares in companies like Nvidia and Adobe despite significant market downturns for these firms. The ARK Innovation ETF has seen substantial losses and outflows, but the firm is betting on a rebound in battered tech stocks. Additionally, there has been a management reshuffle within ARK Invest, with William Scherer taking over two ETFs and Brett Winton promoted to chief futurist.

title: Tesla adds billionaire Airbnb co-founder Gebbia to board
summary: Tesla Inc. has appointed Airbnb co-founder Joseph Gebbia to its board, reversing an earlier plan to reduce the number of directors. This move follows criticism from a shareholder group regarding the lack of independent board members and the need to comply with a 2018 SEC consent decree. Gebbia will waive cash and stock compensation for a period, though some experts question whether his appointment truly adds diversity to the board.

title: CATL – The Battery Giant Leading Innovation in China A-Shares
summary: This article highlights Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL), the world's largest EV battery supplier, founded by Yuqun Zeng. Despite its global importance, CATL, trading on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, is often inaccessible to international investors, but the KraneShares Bosera MSCI China A-Share ETF (KBA) includes it as a top holding. The company's success is attributed to its technological innovation, supply chain advantages within China, and efficient manufacturing processes, positioning it as a leader in the rapidly expanding EV battery market.

title: CATL – The Battery Giant Leading Innovation In China A-Shares
summary: Contemporary Amperax Technology Co., Limited (CATL) is a leading innovator and one of the largest EV battery suppliers globally, providing batteries for major companies like Tesla, Ford, and NIO. Due to its listing on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, CATL is often inaccessible to international investors through standard brokerage accounts and ETFs, making the KraneShares Bosera MSCI China A-Share ETF (KBA) a key avenue for investment access. The article highlights CATL's significant role in the EV market and its founder's origin story.

title: The Rivian R1T Is the Best Truck I’ve Ever Driven
summary: The author reviews the Rivian R1T electric pickup truck after taking it on an off-roading, backcountry camping trip. He highlights its impressive off-road capabilities, luxury features, and storage, acknowledging its "game changer" status despite challenges like range anxiety and a high price point. The article concludes that while expensive, the R1T delivers an outstanding driving and outdoor adventure experience.

title: Here are the people who texted Elon Musk to offer advice or money for the Twitter deal
summary: This article details text messages between Elon Musk and various tech and media luminaries concerning his bid to buy Twitter. The exchanges reveal advice, investment offers, and discussions about the platform's future, as shared in court documents related to Musk's attempt to back out of the $44 billion acquisition. Notable texters include Jack Dorsey, Larry Ellison, Joe Lonsdale, and Sam Bankman-Fried.

title: TTAC: Overweight Tech & Energy, Underweight Industrials & Communication
summary: The FCF US Quality ETF (TTAC) focuses on free cash flow to select approximately 150 stocks, aiming to outperform the Russell 3000. As of late August, TTAC was overweight in technology and energy sectors and underweight in industrials and communication services. FCF Advisors prioritizes free cash flow metrics, which they believe are more difficult to manipulate than GAAP earnings, especially in the current challenging investment environment.

title: Tesla Gets a Warning From NIO, Li, XPeng Deliveries
summary: Deliveries from Chinese electric vehicle makers NIO, XPeng, and Li indicate a warning for Tesla as their growth lags behind the overall industry. The article suggests that car buyers are drawn to new models, potentially impacting Tesla's market share. This trend highlights the importance of innovation and new product offerings in the EV market.

title: How John Deere plans to build a world of fully autonomous farming by 2030
summary: John Deere aims to achieve fully autonomous farming by 2030, building on two decades of investment in AI and robotics, including its autonomous 8R farm tractor. Despite current fleet size being under 50 units, the company is making strategic acquisitions and partnerships to advance its technology. Competitors like AGCO and Case IH are also developing autonomous solutions, with AGCO focusing on retrofit kits for existing machinery and Case IH recently unveiling its autonomous Trident 5550 applicator.

title: Tesla's a 'key stock in everyone’s ESG portfolio.' So why is that so controversial?
summary: This article examines the controversy surrounding Tesla's inclusion in ESG portfolios despite its environmental contributions. While Tesla is a leader in EV technology and carbon emission reduction, concerns about its corporate governance, transparency on emissions, and controversies like racial discrimination and Autopilot safety issues have led to scrutiny and even removal from certain ESG indices. This highlights a fundamental debate within the ESG investing world regarding what constitutes true social responsibility and impact.

title: Tesla slides on widening delivery and production gap, demand worries
summary: Tesla Inc. shares dropped 8.6% due to lower-than-expected third-quarter deliveries, attributed to logistical challenges and growing concerns about demand amidst rising prices and economic slowdown. Despite record deliveries, the significant gap between production and deliveries highlighted transport issues, impacting Tesla's market value and raising questions about future sales. Analysts, however, anticipate robust manufacturing margins for Tesla, while rival Rivian reported increased production.

title: Can Vietnam’s VinFast be the Real Contender to Tesla’s EV Throne?
summary: VinFast, a Vietnamese automotive company, is emerging as a potential contender in the electric vehicle (EV) market against established players like Tesla. Despite being a relatively new entrant, VinFast has ambitious goals for production and profitability, offering lower-cost, tech-heavy EVs with comparable ranges to Tesla models. The company is actively expanding its manufacturing capabilities and supply chain, including battery production and semiconductor partnerships, with a focus on penetrating high-wealth Western markets.

title: Cathie Wood bought up Tesla shares after a Monday stock plunge. They quickly rebounded.
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Investment Management LLC purchased 132,213 shares of Tesla on Monday, marking her firm's first buy since mid-June after a significant stock decline. This dip-buying activity led to a quick rebound in Tesla's shares by as much as 4% on Tuesday, contributing to S&P 500 gains. The purchase indicates a renewed strategy of buying the dip after a year of selling down her stake in the EV manufacturer, whose shares had previously lost their "crown jewel" status in her main fund.

title: Micron chooses New York for $100B factory instead of Central Texas
summary: Micron Technology announced its decision to build a new $100 billion semiconductor factory in Central New York, opting against Lockhart, Texas, which had been a finalist for the facility. The move comes with the aid of $5.5 billion in incentives from New York. This investment is part of Micron's larger plan to invest $40 billion in the U.S.

title: Is Tesla seeing a slowdown in demand?
summary: Early signs suggest a potential slowdown in demand for Tesla vehicles, indicated by falling waiting times for deliveries in the US and China and the company building more EVs than it delivered in Q3 2022. Analysts note increasing premium pricing and exposure to a decelerating global economy as key factors, while Tesla maintains it still has more demand than supply. The issue of demand and supply balance will be crucial for investors when the company reports quarterly results on October 19.

title: Icahn had Twitter stake worth over $500 mln before Musk's about-face - WSJ
summary: Activist investor Carl Icahn amassed a Twitter stake worth over $500 million in the months leading up to Elon Musk's decision to proceed with the takeover. Icahn, who paid around the mid-$30s per share, made an estimated profit exceeding $250 million after Twitter shares jumped over 22% following Musk's announcement. Other investors like D.E. Shaw Group and Daniel Loeb's Third Point LLC are also expected to see significant gains from their recent bets on Twitter shares.

title: Exclusive: Apollo, Sixth Street no longer in talks to finance Twitter deal
summary: Apollo Global Management and Sixth Street Partners are no longer discussing providing financing for Elon Musk's proposed $44 billion acquisition of Twitter. These talks reportedly ceased months ago when Musk first began to express doubts about the deal. Musk later confirmed that neither entity was part of the announced third-party equity or debt financing.

title: Tesla Stock Gets a Little Good News: S&P Upgrades Tesla Bonds
summary: S&P Global has upgraded the bonds of electric-vehicle maker Tesla, removing their junk status. This development is a piece of good news for Tesla stock investors. The upgrade signifies improved financial health and creditworthiness for the company.

title: Musk says Pepsi to receive Tesla's first Semi trucks in December
summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla is starting production of its Semi electric trucks and PepsiCo Inc will receive the first deliveries on December 1st. The truck, which has a 500-mile range and is expected to cost $180,000, has seen its production timeline pushed back multiple times since its 2017 unveiling. PepsiCo had reserved 100 of these trucks to reduce fuel costs and fleet emissions.

title: Tesla Aims to Deliver First Semitrailer Trucks in December to PepsiCo
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced plans to deliver the first all-electric semitrailer truck to PepsiCo in December, five years after its initial reveal. The truck is expected to have a 500-mile range on a single charge. This delivery marks a significant step for Tesla's long-delayed Semi project.

title: PepsiCo confirms Tesla Semi truck deliveries to start in December
summary: PepsiCo has confirmed it will be the first company to receive Tesla Semi truck deliveries, starting December 1st. The electric trucks will be deployed at PepsiCo's Frito-Lay plant in Modesto, California, and its PepsiCo beverages factory in Sacramento, as part of the company's efforts to reduce fuel costs and emissions. Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced production of the Semi truck, which boasts a 500-mile range, after years of delays.

title: Tesla's China-made sales hit record following Shanghai factory upgrade
summary: Tesla Inc. delivered a record 83,135 China-made electric vehicles in September, following an upgrade to its Shanghai factory. This increase comes despite a challenging economic environment and growing competition from domestic EV makers in China. Globally, Tesla's third-quarter deliveries fell short of analyst expectations, yet still marked a record for the company.

title: PayPal says policy to fine customers for 'misinformation' was an 'error'
summary: PayPal clarified that its earlier policy update, which suggested customers could be fined $2,500 for promoting misinformation, was sent in error and will not be implemented. The company stated that it does not fine users for misinformation and apologized for the confusion caused by the update, which had gone viral and drawn criticism from former PayPal executives.

title: TVA, VW to Test All-Electric Mobile Drone Response Vehicle
summary: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) and Volkswagen (VW) are collaborating to test an all-electric "Mobile Drone Response Vehicle" based on the VW ID.4. This modified SUV will be used by TVA's drone response team to inspect and maintain over 16,000 miles of transmission lines, supporting TVA's goal to convert its entire passenger car fleet and half of its cargo vehicles to EVs by 2030. The initiative aims to accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles and decarbonize the nation's transportation network.

title: PayPal says policy to fine customers for 'misinformation' was an 'error'
summary: PayPal clarified that a recent policy update suggesting fines for misinformation was an error and never intended to be implemented. The company faced significant backlash on social media, leading its shares to drop, and prominent figures like former president David Marcus and co-founder Elon Musk criticized the policy. PayPal apologized for the confusion caused by the incorrect information.

title: Pepsi first in line for Tesla semi truck deliveries starting in December
summary: Five years after its unveiling, the Tesla semi truck is finally set for delivery, with Pepsico Inc. being the first recipient in December. Pepsico has reserved 100 semi trucks and plans to have 15 on the road by year-end. This development follows Tesla's prioritization of other models due to supply shortages and is boosted by the Inflation Reduction Act's tax incentives for heavy-duty electric trucks.

title: General Motors launches electric grid division
summary: General Motors has launched a new division called GM Energy, signaling the auto industry's strategic goal of fusing electric cars with the electric grid. This new unit will offer a comprehensive suite of energy services, including bi-directional charging, vehicle-to-home capabilities, stationary storage, and microgrid solutions, positioning GM to compete with companies like Tesla in the broader battery and energy market. The initiative aims to address challenges with grid infrastructure, energy storage, and management, with plans for dealerships to promote these new energy products and vehicles to serve as aggregated resources for utilities.

title: Hertz False-Arrest Claimants Can Sue in State Court, Judge Rules
summary: A US Bankruptcy Judge has ruled that over 60 people accusing Hertz of false arrest can join a lawsuit against the company in state court, rather than being confined to bankruptcy court. This decision allows more than 120 individuals to sue Hertz outside of bankruptcy, potentially leading to higher litigation costs and significant jury verdicts for the rental car giant. Hertz, which has appealed an earlier ruling, continues to offer settlements to some alleged victims while fighting other claims.

title: Tesla Plans to Deliver Semis to Pepsi Years After Unveiling
summary: Tesla is set to deliver its first Semi trucks to PepsiCo Inc. on December 1, five years after the electric big rigs were initially unveiled by Elon Musk. PepsiCo confirmed it will take delivery of 15 of the 100 reserved trucks by year-end, which will be deployed at its Frito-Lay and beverage plants in California. The delivery follows production delays due to prioritizing other Tesla models and supply chain issues, with renewed urgency fueled by new federal tax credits for heavy-duty electric trucks.

title: Winter is Coming
summary: S&P Global Mobility warns that the global auto industry faces significant risk from the looming European energy crunch, particularly due to skyrocketing energy prices. This could lead to extensive pressure on OEMs and suppliers with energy-intensive manufacturing processes, potentially reducing European final-assembly plant output by over 1 million units per quarter starting in Q4 2022. The report highlights potential supply chain disruptions, increased energy costs per vehicle, and varying impacts on European countries based on their energy mix, storage, and governmental fiscal positions.

title: GM takes on Tesla in home and commercial energy storage, management
summary: General Motors is launching a new unit, GM Energy, to compete with Tesla in the home and commercial energy storage and management market. GM Energy will offer stationary storage batteries, solar panels, and hydrogen fuel cells, bundling existing public charging services with new residential and commercial offerings. This expansion leverages GM's expertise in batteries, manufacturing, and connectivity, aiming for a significant share in the estimated $120-$150 billion energy management market.

title: General Motors takes on Tesla with new energy division
summary: General Motors is launching a new unit called GM Energy to offer energy storage and management services to residential and commercial customers, directly competing with Tesla's established energy business. GM Energy will provide EV chargers, stationary batteries, solar panels, and hydrogen fuel cells, with Ultium Home services starting in late 2023. The company aims to leverage its core competencies in vehicles and batteries to tap into a multi-billion dollar energy management market.

title: General Motors is launching its own energy storage service, GM Energy
summary: General Motors (GM) is launching a new energy storage service called GM Energy, which will offer residential and commercial customers services like stationary storage batteries, solar panels, and hydrogen fuel cells, similar to Tesla's offerings. The service will bundle public charging with "Ultium Home" and "Ultium Commercial" units, and GM expects to begin sales of Ultium Home boxes in late 2023. GM also plans to team up with SunPower Corp for solar panels and allow businesses to sell energy back to utilities during peak consumption.

title: Why CATL Is the Global EV Battery Leader and How to Gain Exposure
summary: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Ltd (CATL) is the global leader in electric vehicle batteries, supplying major brands like Tesla, NIO, and Ford. The Chinese company, founded by Yuqun Zeng, has leveraged innovation and China's dominance in battery-grade metal refining to become a powerhouse in the rapidly growing EV market. Investors can gain exposure to CATL through various KraneShares ETFs, including KBA, KARS, and KGRN.

title: Honda to build JV U.S. battery plant, retool Ohio plants
summary: Honda Motor Co Ltd and LG Energy Solution announced Ohio as the location for their $4.4 billion joint-venture battery plant, with an initial investment of $3.5 billion and 2,200 jobs. Additionally, Honda will invest $700 million to retool three of its Ohio plants, adding 300 new jobs to boost electric vehicle production. This move aligns with broader U.S. efforts to encourage domestic EV and battery manufacturing through tax incentives and aims to support Honda's goal of 100% EV and fuel cell vehicle sales by 2040.

title: Valkyrie to Liquidate Bitcoin Balance Sheet ETF After Limited Uptake
summary: Valkyrie Funds announced the liquidation of its Bitcoin Balance Sheet Opportunities ETF (VBB) due to limited investor uptake. The fund, which included companies like Tesla and MicroStrategy, will be liquidated by the end of October and delisted from Nasdaq, with investors receiving cash redemption. VBB had only about $570,000 in net assets under management and underperformed the S&P 500 significantly.

title: Northeast embraces first-of-a-kind virtual power plant
summary: Sunrun announced that its virtual power plant, comprising 5,000 home solar and battery systems across four New England states, successfully exported power to the grid this summer, reducing energy demand and reliance on natural gas plants. This program marks New England as the first regional energy market to utilize such a virtual power plant, demonstrating its viability in multistate power markets. Virtual power plants like Sunrun's offer benefits by providing grid resilience, reducing costs for customers, and potentially replacing inefficient "peaking" natural gas plants.

title: Vale’s base metals chief vows to turn around underperforming Sudbury nickel mines
summary: Deshnee Naidoo, the new head of Vale SA's base metals group, is committed to revitalizing its struggling Canadian nickel operations, particularly in Sudbury. The goal is to capitalize on the growing demand for EV battery minerals, with plans including staffing changes, increased exploration, and efficiency improvements, alongside a $945-million expansion of the Copper Cliff mine. Vale is also considering a new refinery in Quebec to process battery-grade nickel, while the company weighs options for its base metals unit's long-term future.

title: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy gets a surprise endorsement from Twitter's soon-to-be owner Elon Musk
summary: Elon Musk revealed on Twitter that his recent weight loss was partly due to using Novo Nordisk's Wegovy, an injectable GLP-1 drug for chronic weight management. This unexpected endorsement provides free advertising for Novo Nordisk, although it raises questions about the drug's appropriate usage. Wegovy is poised to become a blockbuster obesity drug despite potential competition from Eli Lilly's tirzepatide.

title: 7 Things to Know About the God Bless America (YALL) ETF
summary: The God Bless America ETF (YALL) is a new exchange-traded fund designed to invest in "anti-woke" companies that avoid "left-leaning statements" unrelated to their businesses. The ETF prioritizes valuation metrics like P/E ratios and job growth, with Tesla (TSLA) and Nvidia (NVDA) as its top holdings. It will have an expense ratio of 0.65% and hold 30-40 U.S.-listed companies with market capitalizations over $1 billion.

title: Why Tech Won’t Give Up on Silicon Valley, Despite Rising Regulation
summary: Despite a trend of major tech companies relocating out of California in 2020-2021 due to rising regulation, entrepreneurship in Silicon Valley continues to thrive. Companies like Palantir, Oracle, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, and Tesla moved their headquarters, sparking concerns about the region's long-standing dominance. However, the article suggests that Silicon Valley remains a vibrant hub for technological innovation.

title: Gartner Top 10 Tech Trends For 2023: Metaverse, AI, Cloud
summary: Gartner has released its top 10 technology trends for 2023, focusing on themes like optimizing resilience, scaling solutions, and pioneering new opportunities amidst economic uncertainty. The trends include the metaverse, super apps, adaptive AI, industry cloud platforms, and sustainability, emphasizing technology's role in addressing global challenges and driving business value beyond just cost savings. Each trend is accompanied by an example of its real-world application.

title: New Sony-Honda Venture to Compete in Premium EVs with Software Prowess
summary: Sony Honda Mobility, a new venture between Sony and Honda, announced plans to deliver high-end electric vehicles (EVs) by 2026. The company aims to differentiate itself in the competitive luxury EV market by focusing on software, offering advanced features like automation, personalization, and metaverse connectivity. Despite being a latecomer, Sony Honda Mobility seeks to challenge established players like Tesla and European automakers by leveraging Sony's sensor technology and collaborative partnerships.

title: Which companies are making solar panels in the United States?
summary: This article provides an updated overview of companies manufacturing solar panels in the United States as of late 2022. It details how the Inflation Reduction Act's manufacturing tax credits are expected to revitalize domestic solar production, which had been largely reduced to module assembly. The piece lists numerous companies with their current operations, expansion plans, and capacity figures, highlighting their responses to the new federal incentives.

title: Krispy Kreme: The doughnut company continues its revival
summary: Krispy Kreme is partnering with McDonald's to test selling its doughnuts in nine Kentucky locations, signaling a continued revival for the company. After facing challenges post-IPO, including accusations of "channel stuffing," Krispy Kreme was taken private in 2016 and adopted a "hub and spoke" model to ensure product freshness. This strategy has proven successful, with sales projected to reach $1.5 billion this year, tripling 2015 figures.

title: Tesla Sales Rise, but Revenue Still Lower Than Expected
summary: Tesla Inc. reported third-quarter revenue of $21.5 billion, falling short of analysts' estimates despite a 56% rise in sales. The company's shares declined as CEO Elon Musk acknowledged economic headwinds impacting demand and delivery challenges, though he remained confident about Q4 performance and future growth targets. Tesla is also pursuing a share buyback and building a lithium refinery to secure its supply chain.

title: Tesla stock down on growth worries
summary: Shares of Tesla Inc sank after Wall Street analysts expressed concerns that the electric carmaker's growth momentum may be hindered by rapid inflation and logistical challenges, causing several brokerages to cut price targets. Investors are also watching for signs of cooling consumer demand in the face of surging inflation and rising interest rates, which could impact Tesla's delivery growth targets. Despite these concerns, some analysts remain optimistic about Tesla's long-term prospects due to the global shift towards electric vehicles.

title: Tesla cars will not be approved as fully self driving this year, Musk says
summary: Elon Musk has stated that Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) software will not receive regulatory approval in 2022, indicating that the company cannot yet guarantee its cars can operate without human oversight. Despite plans to release an upgraded FSD software by year-end that allows for largely autonomous drives, regulatory approval is still a hurdle. Analysts suggest that the primary issues are both regulatory scrutiny from bodies like NHTSA and the inherent complexity of the autonomous driving technology itself.

title: Industronics’ Executive Director Datuk Chu acquires around 10% of HK-based renowned stocking firm
summary: Industronics Berhad's Executive Director, Datuk Chu Boon Tiong, has personally acquired a 10% stake in Hong Kong-based Bluemount Financial Group Limited, coinciding with Industronics' own postponed acquisition interest in the firm. Another company, Tesla Technology Holdings Limited, also acquired a 26.08% stake in Bluemount, with the condition that Bluemount apply for listing on the London Stock Exchange's Main Market by the end of the year. Datuk Chu will join Bluemount's Board of Directors to lead its expansion in Southeast Asia, focusing on asset management, fund management, and IPO services.

title: BMW plans $1.7 billion investment in US electric vehicle production
summary: BMW Group announced a $1.7 billion investment in its US operations to boost electric vehicle and battery production. This includes $1 billion for its existing Spartanburg, South Carolina factory and $700 million for a new battery-assembly facility in Woodruff. The company also secured a deal with Envision AESC to build a battery cell factory in South Carolina to supply BMW plants, aligning with BMW's strategy to electrify its vehicle lineup.

title: ARK Buys the Dip in Tesla, Shows Strength in Active Management
summary: ARK Invest's Cathie Wood increased the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK)'s position in Tesla (TSLA) by buying the dip after the stock declined to a 52-week low. This move demonstrates the advantage of active management. ARKK is an actively managed ETF that invests in companies relevant to disruptive innovation, including those in DNA technologies, automation, AI, and fintech.

title: AFT celebrates over 180 million MIM automotive turbocharger vanes
summary: AFT, a member of ARC Group Worldwide, has produced over 183 million turbocharger vanes using Metal Injection Moulding (MIM) technology since 2001. These vanes, made for Garrett Motion and used by major automotive brands, must withstand extreme temperatures and are produced from HK30 steel alloy. The MIM process offers speed, minimal material loss, and a significant cost advantage compared to precision casting for these and other automotive components.

title: United Airlines, Netflix, Tesla: Stocks That Defined the Week
summary: This article highlights seven major companies whose stocks experienced significant movement based on recent news. It specifically mentions United Airlines, Netflix, and Tesla as key players, with United Airlines showing a 2.71% increase. The piece suggests that resilient demand is expected to drive profits for companies like American Airlines through year-end, despite economic concerns.

title: Lucid Motors opens factory in Saudi Arabia, tightening energy ties with China
summary: Lucid Motors has opened a factory in Saudi Arabia, with the Saudi Public Investment Fund owning a majority stake. This move is part of Saudi Arabia's National Industry Strategy to diversify its economy away from oil by manufacturing 150,000 EVs by 2026. The article highlights that while Lucid may appear American, it has significant Chinese investment and aims to compete with Tesla in the Chinese market. It also touches on concerns regarding the treatment of migrant workers in Saudi Arabia's labor force.

title: Tesla Cuts China Prices, Partly Reversing Previous Increases
summary: Tesla has reduced prices for its electric vehicles in China, with cuts ranging from approximately 5% to 9% on its locally built Model 3 and Model Y. This move comes as competitive and economic pressures are intensifying in the Chinese market, leading to a drop in Tesla's shares to their lowest point since June of the previous year. The company's management also anticipates falling short of its growth targets for the current year.

title: ICL Group to build LFP cathode-material manufacturing plant in St. Louis
summary: ICL Group plans to build a $400-million lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode active material (CAM) manufacturing plant in St. Louis, which will be the first large-scale LFP material manufacturing plant in the United States. The company received $197 million in funding through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and expects the plant to be operational by 2024, producing 30,000 metric tons annually by 2025. This initiative aims to strengthen domestic supply chains for the growing EV and battery industries.

title: Panasonic to source graphite from North America
summary: Panasonic has signed an MoU with Nouveau Monde Graphite (NMG) to establish a North American supply chain for graphite, a critical material for lithium-ion batteries. This move is driven by increasing electric vehicle demand and the need to localize sourcing, possibly influenced by the US Inflation Reduction Act. The partnership with NMG and Mitsui aims to secure responsibly sourced graphite from Quebec, aligning with Panasonic's carbon reduction goals.

title: Lawsuit alleges Tesla HR, managers ignored ‘obscene and misogynistic’ music at work
summary: A former Tesla employee has filed a lawsuit alleging that the company's HR department and managers ignored "obscene and misogynistic" music at a Nevada worksite, leading to a sexually hostile work environment. The plaintiff claims Tesla violated Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 by failing to address her repeated complaints about the music, sexual remarks, stalking, and unwanted touching, ultimately forcing her to resign. The case highlights crucial requirements for HR professionals to address harassment promptly and appropriately to avoid employer liability.

title: Tesla Is No Longer Alone in the Electric Vehicle Race
summary: Tesla, once the sole leader in the electric vehicle (EV) market, now faces significant competition from well-established automakers like General Motors, Ford, and Mercedes-Benz. As more than a dozen new EVs are set to launch, analysts predict Tesla's market share will decline considerably by 2025. Despite CEO Elon Musk's optimism, concerns about demand, driven by economic downturns and increased interest rates, have led to price cuts in China and left analysts uneasy about Tesla's near-term outlook.

title: Wix Becomes An Official React Native Partner
summary: Wix.com Ltd. has announced its new status as an official partner of React Native (RN), an open-source UI software framework. This partnership signifies Wix's increased commitment to promoting open-source programming and advancing the RN framework by contributing its expertise and extensive RN codebase. Wix joins other major tech companies like Meta and Microsoft in shaping the future of React Native, which is used to build cross-platform mobile applications.

title: Toyota Motor unveils bZ3 all-electric sedan for Chinese market
summary: Toyota Motor has unveiled the bZ3, its second all-electric model, developed specifically for the Chinese market in collaboration with BYD and FAW Toyota. This medium-sized sedan, featuring BYD's LFP battery and Toyota's electrification technologies, boasts a CLTC-rated range of over 600km and will compete with models like the Tesla Model 3. Its design emphasizes family comfort and aerodynamic efficiency.

title: General Motors CEO stresses EV sales progress in shareholder message
summary: General Motors CEO Mary Barra's message to shareholders highlighted significant progress in EV sales and outlined the company's strategy for an electric future. Despite global supply chain issues, GM posted an impressive earnings report with a double-digit profit margin and aims to rapidly grow EV volumes with upcoming models like the Chevrolet Equinox EV and GMC Sierra EV, focusing on high-volume, lower-priced options and vertical integration.

title: Creepy deepfake of Elon Musk tied up and held hostage goes viral
summary: A deepfake video of Elon Musk tied up and held hostage, created by reAlpha Tech Corp as an advertisement, has gone viral. The real-estate startup aims to get Musk's attention to join their board, highlighting the growing concern over convincing deepfakes and their ethical implications, further underscored by Scarlett Johansson's past experiences. The video also features a photoshopped Jeff Bezos.

title: Tesla faces U.S. criminal probe around self-driving claims
summary: U.S. prosecutors are investigating if Tesla misled the public about its Autopilot driver assistance system's capabilities, according to Reuters reports. This criminal probe from the Justice Department's Washington and San Francisco offices began last year and is ongoing. The Autopilot feature is crucial to Tesla's marketing and customer attraction efforts, with CEO Elon Musk stating that solving full self-driving technology is critical to Tesla's valuation.

title: Mobileye pops more than 37% in market debut after spinning out of Intel
summary: Mobileye, Intel's self-driving car technology company, saw its shares surge over 37% in its stock market debut after spinning out of Intel. The IPO, which valued Mobileye at around $17 billion, raised $861 million, with Intel planning to use some proceeds to build chip factories. This market debut provides a notable tech IPO in a slow year, despite Mobileye's valuation being below Intel's initial expectations.

title: Tesla faces U.S. criminal probe over self-driving car claims, sources say
summary: Tesla is under a previously undisclosed U.S. criminal investigation regarding claims that its electric vehicles can drive themselves. The probe by the U.S. Department of Justice began last year following over a dozen crashes, some fatal, involving Tesla's Autopilot driver assistance system. Prosecutors are examining whether Tesla misled consumers, investors, and regulators about the capabilities of its technology.

title: Hertz revenue jumps 12% on car rental demand
summary: Hertz Global Holdings Inc. reported a 12% increase in quarterly revenue to $2.5 billion, driven by strong demand for rental cars due to surging leisure travel and limited new car production. The company's net income rose only 1% to $577 million due to elevated maintenance costs. Hertz is also expanding its electric vehicle fleet, aiming for 25% by the end of 2024, noting 50% lower maintenance costs on EVs.

title: How Farley's plan is going two years in as Ford CEO — and why 2023 is crucial
summary: Jim Farley's Ford+ plan, initiated two years ago, aims to transform Ford into a leader in electric and digitally connected vehicles by focusing on scaling EV production, enhancing software capabilities, and leveraging the commercial vehicle business, all while improving quality. Experts believe 2023 will be a critical year for execution, as the company faces a competitive market, economic uncertainties, and persistent quality issues despite significant progress in its EV strategy and talent recruitment. The plan involves substantial investments in electrification, a split into separate combustion and EV units, and ambitious targets for profit margins and EV production.

title: How EVs Are Made Matters, General Motors Sustainability Chief Says
summary: General Motors' Chief Sustainability Officer, Kristen Siemen, discusses GM's commitment to zero-emission vehicles by 2035, highlighting investments in manufacturing, workforce training, and supply chain. The article emphasizes that the transition to EVs is not just about the final product but also about sustainable sourcing and manufacturing processes, supported by legislation like the Inflation Reduction Act. GM aims to educate consumers and provide a diverse portfolio of EVs to accelerate adoption.

title: If ASX lithium shares are soaring, why is the ACDC ETF down 9% in 2022?
summary: The Global X Battery Tech & Lithium ETF (ACDC) is down nearly 9% in 2022 despite strong performance from individual ASX lithium shares. This is primarily because the ACDC ETF is not a pure-play lithium fund; it invests in a broad range of battery technology, electric vehicle, and car manufacturing companies globally, alongside ASX lithium miners. Its diversified holdings mean its performance is influenced by more than just record lithium prices, offering a more stable but less explosive return compared to individual high-growth lithium stocks.

title: Is the 2023 Genesis Electrified G80 a Good Electric Car? 5 Pros and 4 Cons
summary: The 2023 Genesis Electrified G80 builds upon the luxury of its gasoline counterpart, offering enhanced quietness, refinement, and quicker acceleration due to its electric powertrain. While it presents a compelling luxury EV option with impressive charging speeds and emergency power capabilities, it faces challenges such as lag in stop-and-go traffic, limited navigation features, reduced cargo space, and restricted availability to only a few states.

title: TrueCar Releases Analysis of October Industry Sales
summary: TrueCar expects total new vehicle industry sales to reach 1,165,658 units in October 2022, marking a 15% increase from the previous year. The seasonally adjusted annualized rate (SAAR) for light vehicle sales is estimated at 14.6 million, up 13% from October 2021. The analysis highlights a shift in market constraint from inventory to affordability due to increased interest rates and sustained elevated pricing.

title: GM temporarily suspends advertising on Twitter following Elon Musk takeover
summary: General Motors announced a temporary suspension of its advertising on Twitter following Elon Musk's acquisition of the social media platform. The automaker stated it is evaluating Twitter's new direction under Musk's ownership and will continue to use the platform for customer interactions but not paid advertising. Other auto companies, including Ford, Stellantis, and Rivian, are also assessing their ad strategies or have commented on their plans regarding the platform.

title: GM pauses advertising on Twitter after Elon Musk takeover
summary: General Motors announced it is temporarily pausing its advertising on Twitter following Elon Musk's takeover of the social media platform. The automaker stated it is evaluating Twitter's "new direction" under its new ownership but will continue to use the platform for customer interactions. This decision raises concerns among analysts about a potential wave of advertisers pulling out, which could be disastrous given advertising accounts for 92% of Twitter's revenue.

title: S&P Global Mobility Special Report: A reckoning for EV battery raw materials
summary: A new report from S&P Global Mobility indicates that geopolitical upheaval, trade friction, ESG concerns, and a fragile raw-material supply chain threaten the expansion of EV battery production. Soaring prices of critical battery metals are impacting profit margins and increasing component costs. The report highlights China's dominant role in materials refining and battery cell assembly, while other nations struggle to keep pace, creating challenges for the global transition to electric vehicles.

title: Blink Charging creates an effortless EV charging experience with new Plug&Charge tech
summary: Blink Charging is launching new Plug&Charge technology in partnership with Hubject to streamline the EV charging process, removing the need for apps or RFID cards. This move aims to make EV charging effortless and encourage further adoption of zero-emission vehicles. The company, which has expanded significantly and received substantial grants, introduces this feature to address range anxiety and simplify the user experience, following similar innovations in the EV charging sector.

title: Casey’s Expands Alternative Fuel Options to Further Sustainability Initiatives and Meet Guest Needs
summary: Casey's General Stores is expanding its alternative fuel offerings, including doubling the number of EV charging stations in the past year and continuing to be a leading retailer of biofuels. This initiative is part of Casey's environmental stewardship efforts, aiming to meet growing consumer demand for lower carbon fuel options and align with long-term sustainability goals. The company also announced plans to add more chargers in 2023, while actively minimizing the environmental impact of its operations through assessments and solar power.

title: Report: Tesla Cybertruck production won’t ramp up until late 2023
summary: A new report suggests that Tesla Cybertruck production might not ramp up until late 2023, meaning mass deliveries would not begin until 2024. This follows Elon Musk's previous announcement of "early production" by mid-2023. The article details the Cybertruck's long development timeline, initial specifications and pricing, and subsequent delays.

title: Lack of graphite could gum up American EV market
summary: The American electric vehicle market faces a significant challenge due to a potential shortage of graphite, a key component in EV batteries, primarily controlled by China. While the U.S. aims for domestic production through initiatives like the Defense Production Act and the Inflation Reduction Act, new mining projects face significant environmental and community resistance, particularly in Alabama and Alaska. Experts warn that a lack of graphite could lead to scrambling for the EV market unless more mines are developed or alternative technologies emerge, highlighting a complex tension between climate goals and local concerns.

title: Vinfast & CATL signed MOU to promote e-mobility
summary: VinFast and Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL) have signed an MOU to collaborate on CIIC (CATL integrated intelligent chassis) skateboard chassis products. This partnership aims to provide VinFast with quick global market access, reduce costs, and improve EV performance through advanced battery technology. The collaboration also helps CATL expand its footprint and promotes new EV technologies.

title: Casey’s alternative fuel choices expand; new EV charging stations
summary: Casey’s General Stores is expanding its alternative fuel options by adding new electric vehicle charging stations and promoting biofuels. The retailer now has 134 EV chargers at 28 locations, including 11 Tesla Superchargers. This initiative is part of Casey's environmental stewardship efforts, aiming to provide more lower-carbon fuel options to its customers.

title: 'Strength in automotive' as Ansys looks to grow its simulated software solutions for vehicle makers
summary: Ansys is focusing on expanding its simulated software solutions for the automotive industry, which already represents a significant portion of its annual contract value. The company reported that its automotive customers contributed over $65 million, or 16%, to its annual contract value during the third quarter of 2022. This growth comes amidst other developments in the autonomous vehicle and tech sectors.

title: Lotus’ Super SUV Targets Self-Driving Fast Laps at Racetrack
summary: Lotus' new electric super SUV, the Eletre, aims to be the first car to complete a self-driving lap of Germany's Nürburgring racetrack. This ambitious goal is supported by the vehicle's standard-equipped ROBO Galaxy autonomous driving platform, which includes deployable Lidar technology and two Nvidia Drive Orin systems processing 508 trillion operations per second. While current regulations prevent full autonomous driving on public roads, Lotus plans to demonstrate the Eletre's capabilities at private facilities like the Nürburgring.

title: Cubic SiC: Tomorrow’s champion for power electronics?
summary: This article explores the potential of cubic Silicon Carbide (3C-SiC) as a reliable alternative to 4H-SiC and GaN in power electronics, particularly in electric vehicles.
